articleTitle: Dispersion Kernel Resampling Time-Frequency Decomposition for Accurate Normal Mode Extraction in Shallow Water
abstract: A dispersion kernel resampling time-frequency decomposition method is proposed to improve the extraction accuracy of normal modes in shallow water. The simulation and experimental data processing results show that this method can simultaneously refine the time-frequency resolution and energy concentration of each dispersive curve. The results were compared with those of the traditional warping transform, indicating that the proposed method is effective and accurate for decomposing and reconstructing normal modes. In addition, this method does not require environment-sensitive parameters and has strong automation and engineering practicability, which will help improve the accuracy and reliability of further passive source localization and geoacoustic inversion.

articleTitle: Three-Dimensional Fast Factorized Back-Projection for Multi-CSAS
abstract: To reduce the multi-circle laminar measurement time for circular synthetic aperture sonar (CSAS) imaging and decrease the computational demand of time-domain imaging, this paper proposes a three-dimensional fast-factorized back-projection (FFBP) imaging method for multi-CSAS. The method obtains multi-circle tomographic echo data using a vertical short array to perform a one-time circular motion measurement around the target at a specific height. Using the proposed FFBP imaging algorithm on tomographic echo data at different heights yields, a series of two-dimensional images can be obtained, which are then fused to obtain a three-dimensional image of the target. The validity of the method is then verified via simulation and experiments in an anechoic pool. This method enables high-resolution three-dimensional imaging of underwater small targets, laying foundation for accurate detection and identification of underwater small targets in real-world applications.

articleTitle: A Novel Adaptive Algorithm Scheme for Shallow-Water Cluster Sparse Acoustic Channels
abstract: Low-frequency and shallow-water acoustic channels show obvious cluster sparsity based on the inter- and intra-modal dispersion characteristics. Thus, adaptive algorithms suitable for the general sparsity may suffer from performance degradation in such channels. To solve this problem, this paper proposes the l<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2,0</inf>-norm shrinkage affine projection algorithm. The proposed algorithm chooses the 1<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>- norm to measure the internal correlation between taps inside the cluster and 1<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf>-norm to describe the sparsity between clusters. Meanwhile, the variable step-size is introduced according to the a priori and a posteriori estimation errors. Simulation results indicate that the decision feedback equalizer based on the proposed algorithm can achieve a lower bit error rate, lower steady-state mean square error, and higher output signal-to-noise ratio in low-frequency and shallow-water acoustic communications.

articleTitle: Underwater Acoustic Target Feature Fusion Recognition Using Multitask Learning
abstract: This paper introduces a feature fusion recognition method for underwater targets based on multitask learning (MTL). Initially, to address the limitations of single-feature input in radiated noise spectrum recognition algorithms, this paper proposes an improved Vision Transformer (ViT) for depth learning underwater target classification. Building upon this, the problem of multifeature fusion recognition is reformulated into an MTL framework, and an optimized feature fusion recognition model is proposed using the multiple gradient descent algorithm (MGDA). The performance advantages of the proposed algorithm is validated on the underwater open source dataset DeepShip, offering a novel approach to underwater target feature fusion recognition.

articleTitle: Research on Underwater Weak Signal Detection Technology Based on Position Judgment
abstract: This paper proposes a weak signal detection technology based on position judgment to address the problem of low signal detection probability under high dynamic and low SNR underwater environments. The technology leverages the continuity of signals and the stochastic nature of noise. Each detection unit undergoes statistical and comparative analysis based on multiple peak judgment values. The signal will appear at the same position in each detection unit if the signal is present. It mitigates the impact of threshold values on the performance of traditional detection technology and reduces the probability of false alarms in the system. Meanwhile, the technology incorporates the nearest neighbor constraint, which improves the system's detection performance for high-dynamic targets. The simulation results show that, under the same false alarm probability, the technology can achieve a 3dB processing gain improvement over traditional detection techniques. The experimental results show that, at a distance of 10 km and an SNR of approximately -28 dB, the technology proposed can reliably detect weak signals.

articleTitle: Study on the Radiated Sound Field of Hydroacoustic Transducer Installed on Carrier
abstract: In recent years, to efficiently control the radiated sound field of hydroacoustic transducers, underwater acoustic equipment for communication and detection tasks must be upgraded. However, because of the relatively close distance between the transducer and the carrier of underwater acoustic equipment, the radiated sound field will be remarkably affected by the carrier, especially for the underwater acoustic equipment that sends and receives simultaneously. The change in the acoustic field of the transducer will greatly impact the acoustic isolation of the underwater acoustic equipment, which will have some adverse effects. Therefore, by calculating the radiated sound field of the hydroacoustic transducer installed on the carrier, this study employs finite element software to build an electric-force-sound-solid coupling model, simulates the acoustic-solid coupling between the acoustic wave of the transducer and the carrier under various carrier conditions, simulates the radiated sound field under various states, calculates the axial diameter ratio of the radiated sound field and the acoustic isolation degree, and summarizes the variation rules. This study addresses the problem of simulation and calculation of the acoustic field radiated by the hydroacoustic transducer when the carrier is installed and is helpful to the study of the sound-solid coupling mechanism between the acoustic wave and the carrier.

articleTitle: Single-Channel Multiuser Transponder System Implementation on a Low-Power Platform
abstract: The underwater acoustic position system is the current mainstream underwater navigation system. A long-baseline underwater acoustic system can perform navigation and positioning for an underwater cooperative target, and the transponder is one of the most important components of this system. This system is highly accurate, small, and convenient to use. However, its battery power restricts its application in ocean exploitation. This paper presents a low-power platform (STM32L4)-based single-channel multiuser underwater transponder system. The system can support up to four cooperative targets for range acquisition. Furthermore, a robust and fast signal processing algorithm based on copy correlation is applied. The sea experiment shows that the system can achieve reliable underwater acoustic ranging in a shallow-water region.

articleTitle: Research on Suspended Sediment Concentration Detection Based on the ISSA-RF Model
abstract: Traditional methods for detecting suspended sediment concentration, such as the weighing method, optical method, and remote sensing monitoring method have high equipment requirements and complex detection processes. To address these issues, a multi-frequency acoustic suspended sediment concentration detection device is constructed. Based on the characteristics of the received signals, the use of frequency domain features is proposed to improve the random forest algorithm for detecting the suspended sediment concentration, namely the Random Forest Based on Improved Sparrow Search Algorithm (ISSA-RF) algorithm. This algorithm enhances the traditional sparrow search algorithm by optimizing its initialization process to mitigate issues related to reduced population diversity and convergence to zero during the search process. Additionally, this improved algorithm is utilized to select the optimal parameters of the random forest, thereby reducing the time required for constructing the random forest model. We use the ISSA-RF algorithm to simulate the detection of suspended sediment concentration, and the results show that the algorithm effectively improves the efficiency of constructing the random forest model and the accuracy of detection.

articleTitle: Coherent Accumulation of Weak Periodic Signals
abstract: Aiming at the problem that existing single-frame detection methods have a short detection distance for black box acoustic beacons, this paper proposes a coherent accumulation detection method for weak periodic signals. This method divides the received signal into frames according to a fixed observation period, predicts the change range of the acoustic beacon emission period when the temperature changes and the observation platform moves, and then performs a small step period search and coherent accumulation according to the predicted period range. The frequency domain compensation method is used to solve the accumulation problem when the search and frame periods are inconsistent and improve search efficiency. The simulation results show that this coherent accumulation detection method can effectively improve the performance of acoustic beacon signal detection under low signal-to-noise ratio conditions. The performance of the 64-frame coherent accumulation detection method was improved by approximately 18 dB compared with that of the single-frame detection method.

Author Keywords: frequency domain phase shift delay compensation

articleTitle: Underwater Target Recognition Based on Multiframe Feature Extraction
abstract: Automatic target recognition by image sonar is a prerequisite for autonomous underwater vehicles that can perform underwater exploration and maritime rescue. In this study, the texture and shape features of underwater targets are studied, and an underwater target recognition algorithm based on multiframe feature extraction is proposed. Experimental results reveal that the proposed algorithm has high accuracy in identifying small targets, effectively enhancing the reliability of image sonar automatic target recognition technology.

articleTitle: Vertical Array Cable Jitter Noise Suppression Method using Frequency Vertical Wavenumber Spectral Filtering*
abstract: The proposed method suppresses low-frequency cable vibration noise in a vertical array acoustic observation system using the frequency vertical wavenumber spectrum. Initially, the frequency wavenumber spectrum is extracted from the data collected from the vertical array via vertical wavenumber-depth transformation. A frequency wavenumber domain filter is designed according to the sound wave speed in the cable, and cable interference is filtered out. The signal is restored via vertical wavenumber-depth inverse transformation. The simulation results show that under the simulation conditions described herein, low-frequency line spectra such as 30 and 60 Hz can achieve a signal-to-noise ratio improvement of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$>1.2\text{dB}$</tex>.

articleTitle: Accurate Time-Delay Vector Estimation for Distorted Towed Array Based on Phase Difference Unwrapping of Line Spectrum Component
abstract: To address the impact of broadband multitarget interference during the signal reconstruction of distorted towed arrays, the phase difference measurements of the line spectrum component in ship-radiated noise are often exploited to estimate the time-delay difference of a target signal received by different hydrophones. Notably, the high-frequency line spectrum offers more precise time-delay difference estimations than its low-frequency counterparts. However, there has always been a problem of modulus 2π ambiguity in the high-frequency line spectrum component, the half-wavelength of which is shorter than the spacing between adjacent hydrophones. Herein, we introduce an innovative technique for estimating time-delay vectors in distorted towed arrays. This method involves unwrapping the phase difference of the high-frequency line spectrum component and leveraging the lattice point theory. The proposed approach enhances the accuracy of time-delay difference estimations and the signal reconstruction performance in distorted towed arrays. The effectiveness and accuracy of the proposed method are validated by simulation results.

articleTitle: Sound-field Prediction Method in Active Enclosed Spaces Based on the Compressed Sensing Equivalent Source Method
abstract: Traditional acoustic holographic measurement method cannot avoid the singular integral caused by an internal source and several measurement points. Considerbaly, the proposed method is based on the compressed sensing equivalent source method and predicts the internal sound field in an active closed space. First, a sound-field prediction model based on the equivalent source method is established through joint modeling of the equipment inside a closed space and its structure. Second, the number of measurement points can be reduced to ensure accurate prediction by introducing compressed sensing theory into the sound-field prediction model. The effectiveness of the proposed method was verified using simulation calculations, and the validity and feasibility were verified using an internal sound-field prediction test of a cylindrical tank model.

articleTitle: Detection and Identification of Anomalous Acoustic Targets in the Sub-Ice Environment of the Arctic
abstract: Based on the analysis of historical underwater noise data from polar scientific expeditions, a substantial presence of impulsive noise is observed. These impulsive noises originate from atmospheric influences on the ocean, dynamic processes in the ice layer, geological activities, volcanic eruptions, marine mammal vocalizations, and human activities. The pulse width, energy, and time-frequency characteristics of these impulsive noises are unknown, and they greatly vary. Research on the characteristics and environmental effects of Arctic noise has been domestically and internationally conducted. However, owing to the complex marine environmental background noise in the Arctic, the performance of traditional detection algorithm has been declined. This paper, based on convolutional neural networks, conducts feature recognition and environmental effect analysis on field-recorded data from Chinese Arctic expeditions and relevant data from foreign sources. It is an important reference for establishing the Arctic noise model, formation of the acoustic transient feature library for specific regions under the Arctic ice, and identification of other acoustic transient signal features.

articleTitle: Research on the Impact of Beacon Turn Around Time in Underwater Acoustic Positioning
abstract: Non-identical positioning phenomena are commonly encountered in underwater acoustic applications during signal transmission and reception. Conventional acoustic ranging observation models typically assume that the underwater platform is stationary and simply use half the two-way propagation delay as a measurement of single-way propagation delay. This study conducts theoretical derivation and simulation analysis to evaluate the approximation errors in acoustic ranging observation models. The effects of underwater platform motions on the non-identical positioning of transmission and reception in acoustic ranging are investigated. The extent and patterns of the effects of acoustic beacon turnaround time on acoustic ranging are also analyzed. Theoretical derivation and simulations indicate that the ranging error, when incorporating beacon turnaround time, increases compared to the ranging error when turnaround time is not considered. The absolute value of this increase in ranging error is proportional to the acoustic beacon turnaround time and inversely proportional to the relative horizontal (or vertical) position of the underwater platform's trajectory in relation to the acoustic beacon.

articleTitle: HFM-based M-ary Cyclic Shift Keying Spread Spectrum Scheme in Mobile Underwater Acoustic Communications
abstract: In shallow water acoustic communications, the multipath delay spread and Doppler effect can severely restrict communication performance. To address this problem, in this study the M-ary cyclic shift keying spread spectrum underwater acoustic communication (UAC) scheme based on hyperbolic frequency modulated (HFM) signal is proposed. The proposed UAC scheme has higher spectral efficiency and data rate than the traditional chirp spread spectrum scheme. Since HFM signal can provide excellent Doppler invariance performance, robust data transmission without Doppler estimation and compensation can be attained in mobile UAC. The relationship between scheme modulation parameters and the Doppler coefficient is analyzed. Finally, the effectiveness and robustness of this proposed scheme were validated via numerical simulations and sea trials.

articleTitle: The Study of Backscattering Acoustic Field from inhomogeneous Distributed Bubbles
abstract: The finite amplitude sound waves propagate through the bubbly liquids will produce backscattered acoustic waves and nonlinear effects, which are the important acoustic characteristics of bubbles that distinguish them from other suspended scatterers in water. Firstly, the linear backscattering sound pressure containing inhomogeneous distributed bubble water medium is obtained by integrating the linear backscattering cross-section. The backscattering sound pressure level calculated by the fluid medium with different bubble distributions under the same excitation is compared and analyzed, and the excitation conditions and applicable backscattering types that can more fully reflect the acoustic characteristics of bubbles under different distributions are given.

articleTitle: Multichannel Adaptive Low-Frequency Noise Control Based on the Sound Pressure Integral
abstract: Controlling the far-field radiated acoustic field using only a single pressure signal from a submerged target in the near field poses significant challenges. Similarly, the approach of modulating the far-field acoustic field by suppressing target surface vibrations largely depends on the placement of secondary sound sources and error sensors. In this work, we take a specific direction in space as the observation plane and use the joint integral of the sound pressure within a small range near the noise source as the controlled target. The multichannel sound pressure method is employed for directional noise control. The experimental results demonstrate that, compared with single-channel sound pressure control algorithms, multichannel active adaptive control based on a sound pressure integral significantly enhances the low-frequency noise control range observed.

articleTitle: Improved Density-Based Data Association Method Under Azimuth Rate Constraint
abstract: Passive sonar has been extensively researched in recent years. However, bearing-only tracking faces significant challenges because passive detection only provides target information. Traditional algorithms estimate target states using Rao-Blackwellized Monte Carlo Data Association and form target trajectories using clustering and label management algorithms. However, the tracking effectiveness of this method depends on the results of the clustering algorithm, which leads to trajectory discontinuity in scenarios with target trajectory crossings. This study addresses the problem of trajectory crossing in passive scenarios by proposing an improved clustering method and label management logic. The experimental results confirmed that the proposed algorithm in this scenario can accurately estimate the number of targets and achieve robust target tracking.

articleTitle: Easy-Hardware-Implementation Algorithm of Carrier and Sampling Frequency Offset Estimation in OFDM Systems
abstract: This paper analyzes the impact of residual carrier frequency offset and sampling frequency offset on the performance of orthogonal frequency division multiplexing systems. Additionally, it proposes a joint carrier and sampling frequency offset estimation algorithm in the frequency domain. The algorithm is designed for easy implementation in hardware, aiming to reduce both the utilization of hardware resources and calculation delays compared to estimation algorithms using the least squares method. Simulations were conducted based on the IEEE 802.11a standard, along with hardware implementations on the field programmable gate array to validate the algorithm. The results of actual system tests demonstrate that the algorithm effectively compensates phase offset, ensuring compliance with standard requirements.

articleTitle: Study on Low-Frequency Small-Scale Longitudinal Transducer with Spiral Spring
abstract: To extend the working frequency band of the longitudinal transducer to the low-frequency band, this study proposes a type of low-frequency longitudinal transducer structure with a spring-mass system driven by the piezoelectric vibrator, which utilizes the piezoelectric vibrator to excite the low-frequency mode of the spring-mass system. In this study, the equivalent circuit of the transducer is given. On the base of the equivalent circuit, the relationship between the source level and the structure parameters of the transducer is analyzed. The finite element model of the transducer is established, and the modal analysis and harmonic analysis are conducted. The theoretical results calculated by the equivalent circuit are in good agreement with the simulation results solved via the finite element method. The virtual prototype realizes low-frequency resonance at 560 Hz with a total length of 0.187 m. The source level in the frequency band of 300–1000 Hz is remarkably enhanced when compared with the traditional structure. The transducer of this structure can produce small-scale and low-frequency resonance, thus expanding the application of the longitudinal transducer to the field of ship-radiated noise simulation.

articleTitle: Analysis of Grey Correlation Method between Underwater Target Orientation and Track
abstract: Currently available underwater target detection systems employ hydroacoustic detection methods for the fusion of water surface and underwater targets, producing unsatisfactory results. To address this problem, the correlation technology of pure azimuth targets and positioning target trajectories was analyzed in this study. Using the grey correlation theory, a grey correlation matrix was established between pure azimuth and target trajectories; consequently, the similarity between trajectories was calculated. This method could effectively correlate radar and sonar data, which assisted underwater target fusion and classification. Accordingly, the accuracy of underwater target identification was improved. Thus, this study provides technical support for the research on target fusion and classification in maritime target detection systems.

articleTitle: Improving Directional Resolution of Ocean Sound Sources Based on Oceanic Boundary Generative Adversarial Network
abstract: The rapid development of artificial intelligence has brought new possibilities to signal processing. In the field of ocean moving target monitoring, traditional array signal processing faces significant challenges due to strong ocean background noise and observation equipment limitations. This paper presents a novel approach for enhancing the directional resolution of ocean sound sources using an oceanic boundary generative adversarial network (OB-GAN). Traditional methods used to analyze underwater sound signals often face challenges in accurately determining the direction of sound sources due to complex environmental conditions. The proposed OB-GAN framework leverages generative adversarial networks (GANs) to learn and enhance the spatial features of underwater sound signals, enabling more precise localization of sound sources. Experimental results demonstrate significant improvements in the directional resolution of ocean sound sources compared to existing methods, showcasing the potential of OB-GAN for advancing underwater acoustic signal processing.

articleTitle: Registration of Hydroacoustic Signals by Coastal Laser Strainmeters
abstract: This study aims to investigate the possibility of registering a source of hydroacoustic radiation by a system of spatially spaced coastal laser strainmeters (LSs) or a two-coordinate LS. The experimental complex includes onshore LS of stationary and mobile versions and low-frequency sonar emitting systems. The method of conducting this experimental work is described, which allows for the investigation of the possibility of receiving a signal at different distances from receiving systems and a moving signal source. Based on the results of the experiment, LSs stably register signals from sources of hydroacoustic vibrations. The results obtained reveal the possibility of registering a source of hydroacoustic radiation as it moves through a controlled water area. In this case, the control can be conducted by combining two different measurement methods: (1) the method of spatially spaced LS and (2) the method of amplitude modulation of the signal of multidirectional components of LSs. The results obtained revealed the prospects of using a system of LS to register sources of low-frequency sonar radiation along the coast of offshore zones.

articleTitle: Optimized Auxiliary Classifier Generative Adversarial Network Model for Underwater Acoustic Source Ranging
abstract: Neural networks have been used for acoustic detection or localization, obtaining remarkable results. However, the size of underwater data has a considerable effect on the accuracy of passive ranging, and the scarcity limits the ranging performance of the neural network. Herein, an optimized auxiliary classifier generative adversarial network (ACGAN) model is proposed. The extensive data produced by the generator network are regarded as extended datasets. The effectiveness of the optimized model was verified using outfield experiment data. With the support of the optimized ACGAN, the accuracy of underwater passive ranging was substantially improved. In addition, the latent space of different datasets is obtained via principal component analysis to measure the authenticity of fake and real data.

articleTitle: Research on Marine Organisms Recognition Method Based on Acoustic Features
abstract: This paper constructs a marine organism recognition model utilizing acoustic features to facilitate long-distance recognition of marine organisms. Initially, the preprocessing method for marine biological acoustic signals is outlined, and the acoustic signals of real marine organisms are transformed into two-dimensional time-frequency images through time-frequency analysis. Subsequently, a recognition model for whales and dolphins, based on a convolutional neural network (CNN) and designed using the PyTorch deep learning framework, is presented. The model undergoes training and testing via the five-fold cross-validation method to establish a recognition model for marine organisms. The results demonstrate that the CNN model achieves a recognition accuracy of 83.67% at a signal-to-noise ratio of 20 dB, thus realizing the objective of recognizing marine biological features acoustically.

articleTitle: Unscented Kalman Filter for Horizontal Circular Array for Tracking Underwater Maneuvering Target Bearings
abstract: Maneuvering target-bearing tracking is one of the most attractive research areas in underwater acoustic signal processing. The horizontal circular array is isotropic and exhibit the same beamforming effect in all bearings, which is better than the linear array under the same aperture. This paper presents an experiment on Qiandao Lake using a horizontal circular array and an unscented Kalman filter to solve the underwater maneuvering target-bearing tracking problem. Compared with the conventional beamforming method, it was verified that the addition of prior models can improve the performance of maneuvering target-bearing tracking.

articleTitle: Under-Ice Delay-Doppler Doubly Spread Acoustic Channel Estimation Based on Compressed Sensing
abstract: The performance of the traditional channel estimation algorithm is extensively degraded owing to the delay-Doppler doubly spread characteristics of the under-ice acoustic channel and the presence of impulsive noise interference. To effectively estimate the delay-Doppler doubly spread channel under ice, this paper adopts an orthogonal matching pursuit (OMP) algorithm based on dictionary reconstruction and the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$l_{p}$</tex>-norm constraint, that is, the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$l_{p}$</tex>-OMP algorithm based on dictionary reconstruction. First, a delay-Doppler domain dictionary is constructed based on the under-ice delay-Doppler doubly spread channel model. Then, the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$l_{p}$</tex>-norm is used to suppress the impulsive noise, and the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$l_{p-}$</tex> OMP algorithm is used to estimate the under-ice delay-Doppler doubly spread channel. The results show that the mean squared error of this method is 0.398, which is lower than that of the traditional OMP algorithm when considering generalized signal-to-noise ratio of -3 dB, and that the under-ice delay-Doppler doubly spread channel can be reliably estimated.

articleTitle: Weak Signal Detection Algorithm Based on Multi-coupled Chaotic Oscillator
abstract: Weak signal detection technology is essential for underwater target detection systems that rely on underwater acoustics. This paper focuses on enhancing the performance of such detection systems. We propose a multi-coupled chaotic oscillator based on the concept of coupling oscillators and analyze its nonlinear dynamic characteristics using phase trajectory diagrams and bifurcation diagram. Subsequently, we develop a comprehensive detection algorithm utilizing this model and refine the system with a variable scale approach. Finally, we created a simulation model to compare the performance of detection algorithms, which includes both single Duffing model and dual-coupled Duffing model, with the existing MCVPD detection algorithm.

articleTitle: Forward-looking Sonar Interferometric Phase Adaptive Filter
abstract: Interferometric phase filters are the cornerstone of sonar for high-precision interferometry. This study focuses on the use of interferometric phase filter for forward-looking sonar, proposing an adaptive short-time Fourier transform filtering algorithm from the perspective of a frequency domain. The algorithm analyzes the image characteristics of forward-looking sonar and proposes a two-dimensional Chebyshev-Kaiser window. The window is determined by the signal-to-noise ratio of the interferogram so that the phase filter can dynamically adjust the filter intensity. The filter reduces interferometric phase noise, thus improving the accuracy of forward-looking sonar interferometric measurement. Simulation experiment and lake experiment show that the filter proposed in this study eliminates over 95% of residues, providing reliable data support for subsequent interferometric phase unwrapping and underwater elevation models.

articleTitle: Analysis of Spatial Characteristics of Sound Field Under the Influence of Underwater Vehicle Wake in Stratified Fluid
abstract: Based on the theory of temperature-density flow, the nonuniform distribution of temperature and salinity in seawater leads to vertical density disparities, which results in the formation of gradient-density step layers. Exploring the wake internal wave field generated by underwater vehicles that traverse these layered structures and understanding its influence on sound propagation can offer valuable technical insights for underwater vehicle detection and tracking. In this study, a three-dimensional model of a specific type of underwater vehicle is utilized to investigate the characteristics of its wake internal wave field. Subsequently, to assess sound propagation loss and the spatial correlation of the sound field under various operational conditions, simulations and analyses are conducted. The findings reveal that both the underwater vehicle itself and the internal wake waves it generates impact sound propagation loss and the spatial correlation of the sound field, with vertical correlation being notably affected.

articleTitle: Theoretical and Simulation Analysis of a New Kind of Quadrupole-Like Transducer
abstract: As one of the common low-frequency high-power transducers, Junas transducers are widely used in the underwater acoustic field. To further reduce the operating frequency band of the Junas transducer, its structure has been changed so that it consists of four radiating surfaces that radiate sound waves outward simultaneously. As a result, the resonant frequency decreases due to increased radiation reactance. At low frequencies, the transducer can be regarded as a longitudinal quadrupole-like acoustic radiation model [1]. From this, the longitudinal quadrupole acoustic radiation impedance is derived, and its rules are analyzed qualitatively. After that, COMSOL Multiphysics, a finite element software, was used to model and simulate it, and analyze the impact of different geometric parameters on its performance. Finally, the rules of the transducer are summarized.

articleTitle: Experimental Research on Acoustic Scattering of Single Fish Target
abstract: The acoustic scattering intensity of single fish target is an important part of fishery acoustics research and is also an important parameter for marine fishery resource assessment. Accurate and timely assessment of fish resources is significant for fishery management and production. Acoustic assessment is an important method to assess fishery resources in water. This article studies acoustic scattering of single fish target through experiments. The results show that the target strength of single fish at different angles has different distribution characteristics. Moreover, the target strength at the back of the fish is smaller than that on its left and right sides, while the target strength in the belly is between the side and the back of the fish. This work can provide reference for acoustic surveys.

articleTitle: The modulation phenomenon of sound speed and attenuation in bubbly media with dual-frequency sound wave excitation
abstract: Bubbles are prevalent in the marine environment, making it crucial to study the acoustic propagation characteristics of bubble-containing water for underwater acoustics and marine science. However, the problem of attenuation and sound speed of bubbly media has not been fully resolved, with most researchers considering it to be time-invariant. Indeed, in the presence of acoustic with different frequency disturbance, the acoustic parameters of a water medium containing bubbles will be modulated by the spatiotemporal alternating sound field. This study presents a theoretical and numerical analysis of the nonlinear modulation phenomenon produced by two columns of sound waves with different frequencies propagating in a bubble-containing water medium. The research focuses on dual-frequency sound waves and establishes a model to describe the instantaneous sound speed and attenuation in bubble-containing water media. The accuracy of the proposed model is validated via a comparison with linear models. The results show that in bubble-containing water medium, the instantaneous sound speed and sound attenuation of high-frequency sound waves are modulated by low-frequency sound waves. This modulation occurs as a result of periodic changes in the bubble radius, which are driven by low-frequency sound waves, the coupling effect of nonlinear vibrations from different frequency components of the bubbles contributes to this phenomenon additionally.

articleTitle: Analytical Solution of Radiated Acoustic Field by Moving Monopolar and Dipolar Sources
abstract: It is challenging to predict the patterns of radiated acoustic field from a complex moving source while this topic is important in the field of ocean acoustics. A possible method is to decompose the complex field into the addition of fundamental sources such as monopolar and dipolar ones. In this study, we derive the analytical solution of radiated acoustic fields generated by a moving monopolar or dipolar source, and the combination of them based on the Lorentz transformation. The analytical expressions of the radiated sound pressure by a moving monopolar or dipolar source are given with no limit on the moving direction and excitation frequency. Numerical simulations are conducted to reveal the Doppler effect of the moving sources and the potential application of the combination of monopolar and dipolar sources to simulate complex fields. This work may help design acoustic models to predict the radiated sound field by complex sources in the field of ocean engineering.

articleTitle: Extraction of Diver Bubble Cloud Feature Using Time-Frequency Spectrogram and Radon Transform
abstract: Recognizing underwater targets is crucial for active sonar. However, there are too many echoes in pulse-echo pitch in practice, resulting in false alarms if some distinguishable features of interesting targets, such as divers, or other targets like ocean creature cannot be extracted from the waveforms or images collected by active sonars. To precisely discriminate the divers from the echoes, an analysis method combined with time-frequency spectrogram and Radon transform is proposed in this paper. Highlighting model describing the bubble clouds and the diver were first constructed. Through short-time Fourier transform, the components of scattering that overlapped in the waveform and were originally difficult to interpret were separated. To characterize the distribution of bubble clouds in the spectrogram, the Radon transform and feature quantity were used. The method was verified by simulation and experiment, and the results show that a diver with bubble clouds can be accurately detected and extracted. Then, the feature used for recognition can remarkably improve the accuracy.

articleTitle: Adversarial Transfer Learning for Underwater Sound Source Localization Based on Horizontal Line Array
abstract: In underwater sound source localization, the lack of abundant training data limits traditional deep learning (DL) methods. Transfer learning (TL) can address the issue of learning with a small number of samples. However, effectively transferring knowledge remains challenging. Moreover, existing DL-based underwater sound source localization methods are primarily dependent on the vertical line array, whereas the horizontal line array (HLA) offers advantages in array aperture and maneuverability. Thus, in this study, an adversarial TL method for underwater sound source localization based on the HLA is proposed. First, the received sound field of the HLA was modeled using the normal-mode method. Next, adversarial techniques from generative adversarial networks were employed, introducing one domain discriminator and two classifiers that collaborate in adversarial training with the feature extractor. This adversarial domain adaptation training aims to effectively transfer knowledge from the model-generated data (source domain) to real underwater data (target domain). Experimental results reveal that the proposed method outperforms several other TL methods.

articleTitle: Spectral Line Extraction in Time-Frequency Representation of Ship Radiated Noise Using Hough Transformation
abstract: To address the challenge of extracting shaft frequencies from the radiated noise of nonco-operative ship targets, this paper proposed a method utilizing an improved Hough transform for lines extraction from the time-frequency spectrum of radiated noise. First, a novel time-frequency representation method for ship-radiated noise is proposed, with the radiated signals being demodulated frame by frame, incorporating time information into the extraction of the DEMON spectrum. Subsequently, the classical Hough transform is modified based on the characteristics of the suggested representation, proposing a continuous voting form of Hough transform for spectral line extraction. Experimental results demonstrate that the presented time-frequency representation and continuous Hough transform can effectively extract spectral lines from ship-radiated noise at low signal-to-noise ratios.

articleTitle: Target Depth Attribute Classification Method with Vertical Linear Array in Shallow-Sea Negative Thermocline Waveguide
abstract: Target depth attribute classification is one of the difficult problems in the field of underwater acoustic information. To discriminate the target depth under conditions of shallow-sea negative thermocline waveguides and vertical linear array, this paper analyzes the formation mechanism of the sound field elevation structure and digs into the differences in sound field elevation angle between surface and submerged targets. A target depth attribute classification method is proposed based on the dependence of the sound field elevation angle on the source depth in a thermocline waveguide. This method extracts the sound field elevation angle as a classification feature and sets the modal elevation angle of the critical mode calculated based on normal mode theory as a threshold. The criterion of surface/submerged target is made through binary judgment. Simulation results prove the feasibility and effectiveness of this method.

articleTitle: Parameter Estimation of Underwater Targets Based on the Auditory Perception Model of Dolphin
abstract: Extracting parameter information from active sonar target echoes can be used to effectively implement underwater target recognition, and dolphin sonar has shown an excellent performance in underwater target recognition. This paper refers to the processing method of underwater signals based on dolphin hearing and investigates parameter estimation of underwater targets based on the auditory perception model of dolphin. The target acoustic scattering echo was processed by the auditory perception model. The radius and thickness estimation of spherical shell were attained using reconstruction methods. Finally, the proposed method was validated experimentally.

articleTitle: Hybrid Protocol Design of Underwater Monitoring Network Based on Cluster Topology
abstract: With the expansion of ocean exploration, underwater acoustic communication technology has gradually matured, and the demand for long-distance underwater information detection and underwater communication interconnection has been on the rise. This paper discusses the application of underwater acoustic communication network technology in the scenarios of large-scale information detection and interaction, proposing the application scenario of an underwater monitoring network. The scenario comprehensively considers the communication needs of underwater sensor information and the surface command center, dividing the network into an information collection network and an information interaction network. According to the work requirements of different networks, this paper proposes a hybrid network protocol. The protocol can balance communication speed and packet loss rate in different network environments and switch modes automatically according to the volume of work to achieve optimal network performance. Additionally, to reduce interference between different types of work, the use of the code division multiple access technology is proposed. By using different spreading codes, this technology reduces communication interference between subnetworks. Simulation testing has shown that the designed hybrid network protocol can meet different work needs and achieve stable data transmission.

articleTitle: Acoustic Scattering Echo Modeling and Signal Separation of Underwater Quiet Small Targets
abstract: In the active sonar detection of underwater quiet small targets, the acoustic scattering echo components overlap, owing to the small geometric size of targets. To solve the problem of mutual interference between rigid and elastic acoustic scattering features of underwater small targets, this paper focuses on the stainless-steel hemispherical cylindrical shell. It examines the separation method of acoustic scattering echo components based on the physical mechanism of the target acoustic scattering, relying on the free-field omnidirectional acoustic scattering measurement experiment. Considering the formation mechanism and signal characteristics of acoustic scattering echoes, the signal models of rigid and elastic acoustic scattering echoes were established, respectively. The energy aggregation characteristics of acoustic scattering echoes in the fractional domain were theoretically deduced and simulated, and then a filtering separation scheme of acoustic scattering echo based on fractional Fourier transform was designed. The results show that by using this method, it is possible to effectively separate and extract omnidirectional rigid and elastic acoustic scattering echoes.

articleTitle: Linear Modulation of the Resonant Frequency of a Double-bubble Model Below an Air-Water Interface
abstract: The study of sound wave propagation across the air-water interface is important for several potential applications, e.g., acoustic communication between underwater environments and air. However, only 0.1% of the power of the incident wave perpendicular to the interface can cross the interface owing to the large acoustic-impedance mismatch between air and water. This renders the propagation of acoustic energy between the media inefficient, leading to the failure of effective acoustic communication between these media. This situation could be solved using designed bubble systems because bubbles are good acoustic impedance matchers. The existing research is mainly limited periodic single-bubble systems, which are not suitable for acoustic propagation in the broadband frequency range. This is because the large sound transmission coefficient between the air-water interface occurs only near a sharp resonant frequency and decreases rapidly away from the resonance. In this work, we propose a periodic double-bubble model below the air-water interface for efficient propagation over a wide frequency range. A numerical simulation model based on COMSOL was developed and validated through comparison with a theoretically analyzed periodic single-bubble system. Then, a periodic double- bubble model was built to study the modulation effect of the resonance frequency versus the vertical interval between the two bubbles. Numerical simulations show that the resonant frequency of the periodic double-bubble system varies linearly with the vertical interval. Therefore this study offers a potential method for designing broadband acoustic communication techniques across the sea-air interface.

articleTitle: Comparison of Waveguide Invariant Estimation Methods
abstract: The waveguide invariant has been widely used in various fields since this theory was first proposed. An accurate calculation of the striation slope is the basis for estimating the waveguide invariant and its application. Radon transform and two-dimensional discrete Fourier transform (2D-DFT) are commonly used to calculate the striation slope. Both methods have their advantages and disadvantages and are suitable for different situations. The effectiveness of the two methods in different situations is discussed in this study. The results show that the 2D-DFT method performs better under low signal-to-noise ratio conditions, whereas the Radon transform method is more suitable when the array is not sufficiently long.

articleTitle: Judging the Birth and Death of Targets in Complex Scenes Based on TBD
abstract: This study proposes a method for judging the birth and death of targets applicable to multitarget scenarios in passive sonar track-before-detect (TBD) scenarios in pure bearing-only. This study first defines target batch variables to manage the labels of multiple targets and establishes a probability model for the joint birth and death of targets based on these variables, providing Bayesian derivation for the model. Using independent partitions (IP), particle filter, and multiple hypothesis tracking (MHT) methods, the target bearing and target batch are sequentially estimated. The proposed method separates the birth and death of a target from the bearing estimation, thus reducing the particle count requirements and improving the computational efficiency. Moreover, this method can obtain trajectories batches and is applicable to various multitarget scenarios, in particular, it remains effective in situations where targets birth or death occur while crossing or are in close proximity. This is the main advantage over existing algorithms. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed method can effectively estimate the target batches in multiple target situations involving the close proximity and crossing.

articleTitle: An Underwater Multisensor Multitarget Tracking Algorithm Based on Particle Filter
abstract: For an underwater passive multisensor multitarget tracking process, where the intersection points of real azimuth measurements include not only real trajectories but also potential “ghost points” that may cause the generation of false trajectories, a tracking algorithm based on particle filters is proposed. First, this study establishes a grid-based association probability model by defining the likelihood function in the particle filter as the association probability of particle states corresponding to measurements from various sensors at grid points. In addition to the correlation probability distribution of “ghost points” in continuous frames being less stable than that of real trajectories, the joint multiframe sum of particle weights is used as the decision criterion for trajectory initiation. Simulation results show that the proposed algorithm exhibits superior tracking performance for multitarget scenarios with missed detections and false alarms, reduces the impact of “ghost points,” and effectively eliminates false trajectories through the joint multiframe decision method.

articleTitle: A Method for Extracting Bubble Features in Multibeam Detection Based on Density Hierarchical Clustering
abstract: Owing to its advantageous features of high resolution, accuracy, and comprehensive coverage, multibeam water detection has gained widespread use. However, challenges arise due to side lobe effects and interference from the water environment, which results in substantial noise within multibeam water images and consequently diminishes the accuracy of target feature extraction. In this study, a gas plume feature extraction method is presented based on density hierarchical clustering, rooted in a thorough analysis of distance and phase characteristics in multibeam water signals. The study begins with an in-depth examination of the principles and noise characteristics inherent in multibeam imaging. To comprehensively reduce noise, an adaptive local threshold segmentation method is employed, which effectively diminishes the impact of noise. Subsequently, to meticulously eliminate any remaining noise, the density hierarchical clustering algorithm is utilized, thereby further enhancing the quality of the water image. The processed water image exhibits a remarkable improvement in quality, concurrently preserving the contour information of plume bubbles. This result serves as a strong validation of the effectiveness of the method proposed in this study. In summary, our research provides a practical technical method for extracting target features in the field of multibeam water detection. The combination of adaptive local threshold segmentation and density hierarchical clustering shows a systematic and effective strategy for addressing noise-related challenges in multibeam water images.

articleTitle: Sonar Waveform Synthesis Based on Mel Generative Adversarial Networks with Self-Attention Mechanisms
abstract: Considering the complicated process of traditional sonar waveform synthesis method, in this study, we apply models from the speech domain to the underwater acoustic domain based on deep learning algorithms using a transfer learning approach. The core of this study lies in the development of a transfer learning framework based on the generative adversarial network (GAN) model, which effectively adapts to the special characteristics of sonar waveforms by fine-tuning the pretrained MelGAN model and the self-attention mechanism. Because sonar waveform cannot be accurately assessed by auditory assessments, we adopted Fréchet Audio Distance (FAD) as an objective audio assessment metric. Experiments based on the DeepShip dataset show that the proposed model effectively synthesizes a sonar waveform.

articleTitle: Research on Large Depth Extension Method of Global Underwater Sound Speed Profile
abstract: Accurately acquiring the sound speed profile (SSP) is essential to the cross-program research on underwater acoustics and oceanography because it plays a significant role in determining the characteristics of underwater sound propagation, reflecting the vertical structure of underwater sound speed and having a significant impact on underwater acoustic networking, communicating, and target acoustic detection. Due to the limitations imposed by the expense of in-situ measurement and the instrument's performance, the SSP measured directly using CTD/XCTD will always have partial or absent depth data. In this study, we acquire the preliminary extension findings of global SSPs with Argo data through a large-depth extension strategy for underwater SSPs. There is a clear reduction in the extension error when compared to the simple average method. The average maximum extension error of global SSPs can be decreased by more than 61%, from 0.071 m/s to 0.027 m/s, when the truncation depth rises from 200 m to 1200 m. In the future, target recognition and underwater sound field prediction can benefit from this research's solid technical idea for the SSP with great depth extension under imperfect depth conditions.

articleTitle: Wideband Signal Direction of Arrival Estimation Algorithm for a Single Vector Hydrophone Based on Data Fusion
abstract: To enhance the performance of direction of arrival (DOA) estimation for a single vector hydrophone in low-signal-to-noise-ratio (SNR) scenarios, this paper proposes a high-precision algorithm based on data fusion. In low-SNR conditions, because of the influence of noise, the estimation performance of different frequency points in the signal bandwidth differs. In this study, the weights are derived based on the least-mean-square-error criterion, and a novel DOA estimation algorithm is developed by integrating the outcomes from diverse frequency points via a data-fusion methodology. The proposed algorithm integrates data fusion into vector hydrophone processing, which results in better DOA estimation performance than the traditional histogram algorithm. Under the assumption of Gaussian white noise, the simulation results prove the efficacy of the method.

articleTitle: Research on the Key Problems of 3D Acoustic Field Modeling and Simulation in Complex Submarine Environment
abstract: The rapid advancements in ocean mapping technologies have significantly improved accessibility to seafloor undulation data, thereby pioneering new avenues for the development of high-precision underwater acoustic field modeling. The present study explored the complexities of sound propagation across a range of depths and frequencies, taking into account the unique characteristics of seabed topographies. To this end, we employed the Bellhop3D model and data from reliable sources such as HYCOM and GEBCO to conduct comprehensive three-dimensional acoustic simulations within complex seabed environments. The research results indicated that the effect of sound propagation is more pronounced in shallower sound sources. In deep, complex seabed, low- frequency sound sources demonstrate superior propagation characteristics.

articleTitle: Low False-Alarm Active Sonar Detection under Strong Reverberation
abstract: In active low-frequency and high-power sonar systems, target detection must overcome strong reverberation. Active sonar reverberation interference strongly fluctuates with distance and exhibits significant temporal and spatial variations. Active sonar reverberation is a typical nonstationary background. Complex changes in reverberation directly affect the target detection performance of active sonar systems. The major difficulty associated with current detection algorithms lies in autonomous detection, particularly in terms of the adaptability of detection algorithms to complex background interference. Accurately performing dynamic background estimation, suppressing interference, controlling false alarms, and highlighting weak targets are the focus of object detection. This paper proposes an active sonar target detection method driven by a combination of data and models. The proposed method can achieve target detection under strong reverberation interference with low sidelobe false alarms and high robustness.

articleTitle: Inversion of Shallow Water Sound Speed Profile Using a Learning-Based Matched-Field Algorithm
abstract: This paper proposes a method for sound speed profile (SSP) inversion in shallow water based on a gated recurrent unit (GFGRU). The K-singular value decomposition method is used to generate a dictionary for the SSP representation. The major tasks of the GFGRU trained on synthetic and real acoustic datasets are multilabel classification and finding basis functions representing the disturbance of the SSP from the dictionary. Next, a genetic algorithm is used to search the coefficients of the basis functions and obtain the inversion SSPs. The performance of the proposed inversion method was compared to the traditional matched-field inversion method, classification results, and final inversion results of the simulation acoustical dataset, driven by the measured SSPs in Shallow Water Experiment 2006, to verify the accuracy and robustness of the proposed learning-based matched-field method.

articleTitle: Simulation of Vertical Highlight Distribution of Underwater Objects Based on Virtual Extended Arrays *
abstract: To study the vertical distribution characteristics of object echo in water, a simulation method based on a large-aperture virtual extended array is proposed. The proposed method adopts the near-field plate element method to predict the object echo waveform at the array end and takes advantage of the high resolution of the large aperture virtual extended array beam. Two-dimensional acoustic images of the object, such as the horizontal-vertical direction, horizontal distance, and range vertical, are obtained. The results show that the object echo highlights of the single-layer shell are obtained three parts of the boat: the hull, shell, and stern, and the vertical distribution characteristics reflect the vertical position relationship of the three parts. The formation mechanism of the echo highlights includes the smooth surface echo of a large area in the hull, hull, and other parts, and the angular wave at the joint of the hull and hull and the hull and stern.

articleTitle: Nonreference Image Denoising for Sonar Images
abstract: Sonar image denoising is critical for high-level postprocessing. However, due to the absence of standardized and clean reference images, most proposed learn-based denoising methods achieve unsatisfactory quality with denoised images. There are variations in the background noise; this variability can improve the performance of the denoising algorithm. Herein, a learn-based denoising algorithm for nonreference images is proposed, considering the differences in noise distribution among sonar images. To obtain relatively uniform and uneven noise blocks, two types of noise block extraction methods are proposed. Then, the denoising model is trained to generate fitted noise maps by these blocks. Finally, by subtracting the fitted noisy image from the input noisy image, a denoised image is obtained. The experimental results demonstrate that the proposed denoising algorithm can achieve comparable or better performance than other compared algorithms.

articleTitle: Research on the Localization Performance of Near-Field Broadband Beamforming Based on Frequency Domain Subband Strategy
abstract: Simulation studies were carried out on the localization performance of three broadband beamforming methods on the basis of frequency domain subband strategy, including broadband conventional focused beamformer (BC-FB), broadband minimum variance distortionless response focused beamformer (BMVDR-FB), and broadband multiple signal classification focused beamformer (BMUSIC-FB), aiming at the passive localization problem of ship radiated noise in near-field environments using uniform linear array sonar. First, the time domain and frequency domain received data models of near-field underwater acoustic signals for uniform linear array sonar were presented. Second, Fourier transform was applied to transform the received data from time domain to frequency domain, and the spatial spectra of BC-FB, BMVDR-FB, and BMUSIC-FB for localization in each subband signal were provided. The spatial spectra of the three methods under broadband signal conditions were obtained through summation operation, and further passive localization of the target was achieved through peak search spectral peak search. Finally, through simulation experiments, the performance of three near-field localization methods is studied.

articleTitle: Three-Dimensional Visualization of Underwater Target by Fusing Acoustical and Optical Information
abstract: Three-dimensional (3D) visualization technology has broad application potential in underwater environment perception, target detection, and other needs. In this study, to make the detected underwater targets more realistic and conducive to human eye observation, multibeam bathymetric sonar and optical sensors are combined to explore a visualization method for the 3D shape of underwater targets. The underwater environment and target 3D point cloud information are measured using multibeam bathymetric sonar and reconstructed using VTK (Visualization Toolkit) for triangulation of the point cloud. At the same time, preprocessing such as color correction and enhancement is conducted on optical images that contain targets underwater. Based on this, by combining the reconstructed 3D model with optical texture images, texture mapping is carried out. The results of the water tank test reveal that the method described in this study can produce good 3D visual effects.

articleTitle: Research on the Cross-Correlation Characteristics of Signals from Ocean Bottom Seismometer
abstract: In this study, considerable differences in waveform between vector signals and acoustic pressure signals were received from the seabed interface. The cross-correlation characteristics between the acoustic pressure and particle velocity signals received via an ocean bottom seismometer were analyzed using experimental data obtained from very low-frequency sound propagation experiments conducted in the South China Sea area. On th basis of the spectral element method, the correlation coefficient of the pressure and particle velocity signals in seawater and seabed interface was simulated and compared with experimental data to validate the cross-correlation characteristics at the seabed interface. Finally, the correlation coefficients between pressure and particle velocity in different types of seabed environments were analyzed. The results reveal that the elastic characteristics of the seabed can have a certain impact on the cross-correlation characteristics of the pressure and particle velocity signals received by an ocean bottom seismometer, which results in a relatively small cross-correlation coefficient between the seabed interface acoustic pressure and horizontal particle velocity signals.

articleTitle: A Multi-node Time Difference of Arrival-Positioning Method Based on Improved Time Delay Estimation
abstract: This paper examines the multi-node localization technology based on time difference of arrival (TDOA), focusing on the impact of TDOA measurement errors on localization accuracy and methods to improve localization precision. First, different localization techniques in various aquatic regions were introduced, followed by a detailed exposition on the establishment of the TDOA model and the application of the Fang algorithm. The importance of time delay estimation for localization accuracy was discussed next, and a method based on multi-channel linear phase for time delay estimation was presented. The effectiveness and accuracy of this method were verified through simulation experiments. In conclusion, the TDOA measurement error is one of the key factors affecting localization accuracy. This paper provides suggestions for reducing TDOA measurement errors and further improvement of localization precision, as well as valuable insights for the development of underwater localization technology.

articleTitle: Ellipsoidal Target Attitude Recognition Method based on Multiple Monostatic Sonar Platforms
abstract: As the demand for active detection of underwater targets increases, the detection task has transitioned from the presence or absence of the detection target to the detailed information of the target. In this study, the highlight model is employed to simulate a single underwater static ellipsoid target, and the attitude angle of the target is identified by comprehensively using the received echo signals of multiple transceiver sonar platforms placed at different angles. Finally, the error analysis of the attitude angle estimation results under different working conditions is conducted.

articleTitle: Nonstationary Noise Estimation Method Based on Spectral Entropy Estimation
abstract: This paper proposes a nonstationary noise estimation method based on spectral entropy estimation to solve the problem of the difficulty of the noise estimation algorithms to track nonstationary noise in time. The method uses spectral entropy and spectral sorting difference to estimate the noise level. It adjusts the smoothing factor when the noise rapidly changes and incorporates a signal presence probability based on spectral entropy as a correction factor in noise estimation. Simulation results show that the proposed method is better than the original algorithm in tracking noise during significant fluctuations. While its retains the advantages of the original algorithm, the proposed algorithm has better accuracy and stability in noise estimation compared to the minimum controlled recursive averaging algorithm.

articleTitle: Research on Ship-Radiated Noise Assessment Method Based on the Force-Sound Reciprocity
abstract: Establishing the transfer function from mechanical vibration to underwater sound radiation is one of the core issues in the assessment of radiated noise from ship machinery equipment. Traditional methods face difficulties, such as limitations of excitation equipment and mutual coupling of vibration transmission. This article proposes a new method for assessing radiated noise from machinery equipment based on the principle of force-sound reciprocity. First, the transfer function is calculated in reverse based on the force-sound reciprocity, and the equipment-radiated noise is then obtained by combining the virtual force method. The verification results of on-site equipment tests show that the results of this method are consistent with the measured radiated noise values, indicating that this method can meet the accuracy requirements for assessing radiated noise under actual ship conditions.

articleTitle: Characterization of Underwater Air Gun Sound Propagation Modes in the Shanwei Region
abstract: This study examines the impact of different seawater and seafloor characteristics on the propagation modes using the fluid-solid coupled modal equation. The dispersion curves show the variations in the propagation modes. The findings suggest that the impact of seawater and seabed density is limited, with the seabed P-wave velocity having a lesser influence and the S-wave velocity having a significant impact. Thus, accurately calculating the speed of sound in the seafloor is needed for dependable modal computations. During the extended transmission of waves generated by underwater air guns, three separate wave packets detected by ocean bottom seismometers (OBSs) correspond to the bottom P-wave, S-wave, and direct water wave. The velocity of sound can be deduced from the times at which these wave packets arrive. A study conducted in the vicinity of Shanwei City has established that the predominant route for air gun propagation is through the first-order normal mode.

articleTitle: Tracking Before Detecting Weak Targets Based on Dynamic Programing in Passive Sonar Scenarios
abstract: In passive scenarios, effective detection and precise tracking of weak targets represent key research directions in underwater acoustics. The traditional detect-before-track method is easy to miss detection in low signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) scenarios. Track-before-detect based on dynamic programing (DP-TBD) has more advantages in handling weak target scenarios. However, in scenarios with target crossovers, there is a risk of trajectory merging, where two target trajectories combine into a single trajectory. This study proposes a speed weight-based method to solve trajectory merging problem. When constructing the value function, adding a speed-weighted function enables the trajectory to be correctly separated in the case of intersection.

articleTitle: Analysis and Application of Array Tilt Influence on Signal Arrival Angle Estimation in Deep Sea
abstract: Previous studies have shown that the vertical line array (VLA) deployed near the seafloor in the deep sea can be utilized to detect and localize source in the upper water column (e.g., within 300 m from the source). Passive localization is based on the relationship between the sound arrival grazing angle and the horizontal distance from the VLA to the source, with estimation of the horizontal distance from the VLA measurements of the acoustic signal arrival grazing angle. In practice, the array tilt will inevitably impact the estimation of the arrival angle and source range. To address this issue, this study analyzes the effect of array tilt on the estimation of arrival angles. It is found that when considering only small angle tilts, tilting the VLA toward the direction of sound source motion results in a rotation of the beamforming output, while tilting the VLA toward the normal direction of sound source movement causes a translation of the beamforming output in the angular domain. Building upon this analysis, a cooperative source-based array tilt estimation method is proposed, and simulation analysis validates the feasibility of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Passive Line Spectrum Detection of a Moving Target With the Fractional Fourier Transform
abstract: To detect line spectrum signals from underwater moving targets, a long-time-integral line spectrum detection method based on the fractional Fourier transform (FRFT) is proposed in this work. This method can mitigate the decrease in the gain of the line spectrum caused by the motion of a target and the resulting Doppler shift. By establishing a mathematical model of the received signal from a moving target, the polynomial characteristics of the phase of the received signal are deduced, and second-order approximate results are given. The polynomial phase signal parameters are related to the parameters of the moving target. Because FRFT can be applied to the integral processing of second-order polynomials, the corresponding processing model and method are given using the FRFT in this work. The actual gains associated with FFT and FRFT for moving targets with different velocities and frequencies are summarized and compared with the theoretical ones. Furthermore, the optimal integration time under different conditions is estimated. Compared with FFT, FRFT lengthens the integration time of the line spectrum of moving signals. The processed results from the simulation data show that this method has excellent line spectrum detection performance at a low SNR and can be adapted to complex situations such as multiple targets and multiple line spectrum signals.

articleTitle: Research on Extraction and Recognition of Acoustic Scattering Characteristics of Underwater Hemispherical Cylindrical Shell
abstract: The problem in the engineering-oriented underwater target recognition reveals that high-quality effective labeled data are limited and the distribution of the target acoustic scattering characteristics overlaps, making target recognition more difficult to carry out. To address this problem, this study employs an underwater hemispherical cylinder shell target as the research object, combines the finite element analysis method to establish the target's acoustic scattering echo simulation model, and analyzes the target's omnidirectional acoustic scattering echo characteristics. Then, the time series structure characteristics of the target echo signal related to its physical properties are extracted. Thus, a target recognition model based on recurrent neural networks is constructed, and the underwater target is accurately identified under limited data via training with simulated data and verifying with actual data. The method of target echo feature extraction and recognition researched in this study can provide technical support for intelligent recognition of underwater targets.

articleTitle: Influence of Immersion Depth on the Sound and Vibration Characteristics of the Line Spectrum of a Partially Immersed Model
abstract: Herein, the influence of submersion depth on the vibration and sound radiation line spectra of underwater vehicles is investigated. In addition, a partially submerged cylindrical shell was analyzed by the finite element method, and the radiated sound power and root mean square velocity curves of the partially submerged cylindrical shell were obtained. For the partial immersion model, when the immersion depth is large, the load difference between the upper and lower parts of the model is small, whereas when the immersion depth is small, the load difference between the upper and lower parts of the model is large, leading to distortion of the vibration distribution of the model with a small immersion depth, and the vibration of the model is asymmetrical, thus causing the line spectrum of the model to shift to a lower frequency. The vibration distortion of the model also caused the vibration of the model to change from a modal vibration to a nonmodal vibration, resulting in disappearance of the line spectrum of the model. For fully submerged structures, changes in the depth of immersion had little influence on the line spectrum of the structure.

articleTitle: Slotted Cylinder Transducer Using an Acoustic-Compliant Material
abstract: Research on acoustic-compliant material is a remarkable for optimizing the acoustic performance of slotted cylinder transducers, and its composition and structure are directly related to the transducer's ability to radiate acoustic waves underwater. Herein, the acoustic wave generation mechanism of the slotted cylinder transducer was analyzed, and the sound source level of the slotted cylinder transducer was compared with that of the overflow structure and air backing. Additionally, an acoustic-compliant material was developed as the backing. A single-component backing made of rubber and an acoustic-compliant material and a composite structural backing made of acoustic-compliant material were proposed. Finite-element simulation and actual underwater measurements were performed. Results demonstrated that under identical size conditions, a single-component backing made of acoustic-compliant material could notably strengthen the radiation capability of the slotted cylinder transducer. Consequently, composite structural backing had less effect on the electroacoustic characteristics. Further encapsulation could strengthen the pressure resistance of the slotted cylinder transducer. Through theoretical analysis, this study explored the material and structure of the backing and further investigated the comprehensive performance improvement of the slotted cylinder transducer using a finite-element software.

articleTitle: Preliminary Analysis of Ambient Noise Level Under Sea-Ice Near the Gakkel Ridge
abstract: The unique geography and distinctive climate of Arctic Ocean provide it with an unparalleled cover made of snow and sea-ice, which has significantly altered the characteristics of its underwater acoustic environment. This study introduced a recent observation of underwater acoustic ambient noise levels and environmental parameters collected from August to November 2021 near the Gakkel Ridge in the Arctic. The data from three different Ice-Ocean Environmental Buoys were discussed, and the statistical characteristics of underwater environmental noise were investigated. After removing the spikes caused by microevents, a sliding window was used to analyze and process the characteristics of underwater ambient noise under the assumption that they are Gaussian, and the results were used to model the frequency distribution of the noise level. Various environmental parameters, both above and below the ice, were used to discuss the possible cause for the fluctuations and variations in noise levels at certain frequency points. The results indicate that due to ice coverage, the ambient noise levels are generally lower than in other marine areas. In the low-frequency range (10–100 Hz), environmental noise levels are mainly concentrated in the range of 60–55 dB, while as the frequency increases (100–2560 Hz), the noise levels attenuate to around 45 dB.

articleTitle: Study on Fluctuation Characteristics of Acoustic Signals under Density Layered Fluid Disturbance
