abstract: This study investigates the fluctuation characteristics of acoustic signals in the presence of flow field perturbations within density-stratified fluids through laboratory simulation experiments. A density stratification tank was used to replicate the ocean's stratified environment. The SUBOFF scaled model was employed to mimic the underwater vehicle's navigation process in towing mode. Controlled density stratification simulation experiments were conducted to explore the acoustic signal fluctuation characteristics within the wake flow field of the submerged model. Data on the undulation properties of acoustic signals that propagated through the wake flow field of the underwater vehicle were collected. The undulation characteristics of the acoustic signal at two towing speeds and various spatial positions were analyzed. In alignment with the typical marine environment characteristics, this study designed the stratification conditions, the scale of the scaled model, and the towing speed based on the Froude number (Fri) similarity criterion and the geometric similarity law. The analysis of the experimental results indicates that the fluctuating frequency of the acoustic signal amplitude diminishes over time as the wake dissipates post-target passage. Concurrently, the intensity of the high-frequency fluctuation component of the signal also decreases with the dissipation of the wake.

articleTitle: Measurement of Very-Low-Frequency Waves Generated by a Heaving Sphere Based on a Vector Hydrophone
abstract: It has long been recognized that underwater vehicles can be detected via gravity waves generated during motion. Therefore, this study aimed to investigate a direct measurement method for surface gravity waves generated by oscillating spheres based on a vector hydrophone. First, based on the principles of linear potential flow theory, the amplitude of the free surface displacement (AFSD) generated by an oscillating sphere in a finite depth fluid is studied. According to the multipole expansion method, the free surface wave characteristics caused by spherical oscillations are numerically analyzed. The surface wave was then tested in a pool. The sensitivity of the very-low-frequency (VLF) vector hydrophone was measured in a water tank, and the AFSD of the VLF gravity surface wave was measured in a pool. The results show that the measured results are larger than the simulation results because of the existence of reflected waves and the influence of the walking mechanism; however, they are of the same order of magnitude. The pool test proved that the vector hydrophone can be used to measure gravity waves and obtain more information than a pressure sensor.

articleTitle: Study on Reliable Acoustic Path Vector Propagation Characteristics of Typical Deep-Sea Trench
abstract: Owing to the unique acoustic channel advantages provided by reliable acoustic paths and the advancements in vector detection technology, the vector propagation characteristics of these reliable acoustic paths in complex deep-sea topographic environments must be investigated for deep-sea acoustic research and detection. In this study, using the sound speed profile and seafloor topography in the South China Sea Trench region as a simulation model, the vector propagation characteristics of a reliable acoustic path were investigated. Our analysis focused on the impact of the trench on both the maximum acting distance and the effective detection distance of the reliable acoustic path. The results reveal that the distinctive topographic features of the trench, characterized by a “from shallow to deep and back to shallow” profile, alter the propagation of sound lines across the trench, which influences the maximum acting distance of the reliable acoustic path. This alteration creates a blind detection zone above the critical depth. Moreover, the trench's topography limits the effective detection distances for sound pressure and horizontal particle velocity across a broad frequency band, with less effect on the effective detection distances for vertical particle velocity.

articleTitle: Underwater Periodic Pulse Signal Detection Based on Coherent Integration
abstract: Detecting weak far-field signals in underwater environments via oceanic engineering is extremely important. Recently, underwater acoustic beacon signal detection has become a popular topic. In this study, the time-frequency analysis of short-time Fourier transform is studied for periodic pulse signal detection, and a long-term multiperiod coherent integration method with a data group alignment technique is proposed. The simulation analyzes the detection performance and delay estimation accuracy of the proposed method. When the integration time or signal-to-noise ratio is limited, the proposed method demonstrates better performance, which is beneficial for practical applications.

articleTitle: Implementation of Target Trajectory Recognition in Bearing Time Recording Based on Deep Learning
abstract: The bearing time recording is widely used in the visible control system of alert sonar, and it has unique advantages, and it is of great military significance to identify suspicious target trajectory attributes in the corresponding bearing. This paper describes a set of deep learning-based methods to identify the target track in bearing time recording. The method primarily includes three technical parts: bearing time recording processing, target track tracking, and corresponding azimuthal target track identification. It also describes a method to automatically scan suspicious target trajectories in an all-round manner. Finally, a hydroacoustic array signal real-time processing, detection, and trajectory recognition system is introduced, which integrates the mainstream hydroacoustic signal processing and analysis algorithms. Simultaneously, the system can also be added to expand the algorithms of other units.

articleTitle: Feature Extraction of the Laplacian Operator Norm for Shallow Water Active Target Depth Discrimination
abstract: This paper proposes a new approach for shallow water active target depth discrimination based on vertical transmitter arrays. Moreover, this paper derives the phase fluctuation of broadband cross-spectrum between the target return dominated by the upper half transmitter array and the target return dominated by the lower half transmitter array to eliminate the influence of target scattering characteristics on active depth discrimination. It is found that broadband phase fluctuation characteristics are strongly correlated with target depth. The norm of the graph Laplacian operator is proposed to denote the phase fluctuation, which shows significant separability for the surface source and submerged source and is independent of target scattering characteristics. Hence, this paper proposes a corresponding depth discrimination method and decision metric. Theoretical analysis and simulation results explain the physical insight of target depth separability and robustness in the ocean environment.

articleTitle: A Method for Resolving Range Ambiguity of High-Frame-Rate Signals Based on Radial Velocity Constraint
abstract: To address the problem of the high computational complexity and low accuracy in traditional majority rule algorithm under high-frame-rate signal conditions, this paper proposes a radial velocity-constrained particle optimization method for resolving range ambiguity. First, by modifying the objective function of the positioning model, the dimension of the unknown parameters was reduced. Second, the particle swarm optimization algorithm was used to search for the optimal position of the objective function within a predetermined range, improving the stability and computational efficiency of resolving range ambiguity. Finally, by integrating an unambiguous radial velocity constraint, the algorithm confines the target location, thereby mitigating the problem of cycle skipping arising from insufficient constraints in algorithms that resolve range ambiguity using only delay information. This enhancement significantly diminishes the likelihood of converging to local optima in the solution space. Simulation results show that the proposed method significantly enhances the performance and stability in terms of resolving range ambiguity.

articleTitle: A Passive Inverted Ultrashort Baseline Scheme for Underwater Positioning Based on the Acoustic Frequency Combs
abstract: In this study, a self-localization method, an inverted ultrashort baseline based on a seafloor four-array base array is designed and implemented to achieve the practical application of autonomous spatial position sensing for small and low-cost autonomous underwater vehicles (AUVs) and reduce the cost of their autonomous localization simultaneously. First, an acoustic frequency comb (AFC) signal with stable time-frequency characteristics and high peak power is designed as the broadband signal. Second, each array element of the four-array base station deployed on the seabed responds with mutually orthogonal AFC signals, and the AUV receives the mixed AFC signals of each array element and then employs the matched filter method and phase analysis method to measure the one-way flight time of each signal coarsely and accurately. Finally, to realize the autonomous position solution of the A UV, the inverted ultrashort baseline positioning method is combined. The results show that the AUV only needs to carry a single receiving beacon to complete its own position sensing, which further reduces the cost and system complexity. Moreover, the results also prove the high reliability of the AFC signal, which can realize high autonomous localization accuracy at the AUV end.

articleTitle: A Prediction Method for Deep Sea Ambient Noise Intensity Based on Long Short-Term Memory
abstract: The intensity characteristics of deep-sea ambient noise are important parameters for the evaluation of the operating distance and signal-to-noise ratio of underwater equipment. This study conducted research on the prediction method of ambient noise intensity based on long short-term memory network. The prediction was conducted on measured deep-sea data in two scenarios, medium-long time scale and short time scale. The results show that under medium-long-time scale conditions, the temporal trend of predicted noise intensity is consistent with the real trend, but in some frequency bands, considerable errors and time delays exist. The mean of root mean square error (RMS) in the frequency band of 20 Hz-5 kHz is 4.31 dB. Under short time scale condition, the average RMS between the prediction and measured is 0.73 dB within the same frequency range. At the same time, the correlation coefficient between the predicted noise intensity curve with frequency and the true value curve is 0.96.

articleTitle: An Improved Broadband Target Localization Method Based on the Equivalent Vector Hydrophone
abstract: The vector hydrophone vertical array is an important form of array used in the underwater target localization field. This paper introduces an improved method for deep-sea broadband passive target localization. The conventional beamforming is initially applied to acquire the elevation angles. Subsequently, these angles are applied to compensate for the phase differences, and the four sub-arrays after compensation are treated equally as a vector element that is processed through the designated spatial filter. The equivalent vector element and spatial filtering processing fully utilize the array gain of the sub-array and effectively filter out the noise and interference from unexpected directions. Thus, the signal-to-noise ratio of the received signal can be improved. The accuracy of the estimated elevation angles and target depth is utilized to evaluate the proposed method's performance. The results of simulation and a sea trial that demonstrate this method can offer benefits of simple computation and high accuracy compared to the conventional method for a single vector hydrophone.

articleTitle: Suppression of Cross-Terms in the Wigner-Ville Distribution of Underwater Static Target Echo
abstract: The echo information components of underwater static targets are intricate and encompass vital details regarding target shape and structure. When the active sonar emission signal adopts a linear frequency modulation (LFM) signal, the target echo comprises superimpositions of multiple LFM signals with varying amplitudes and delays. Although the Wigner-Ville distribution (WVD) serves as a potent tool for analyzing LFM signals, the WVD for multicomponent LFM signals yields numerous cross-terms. These cross-terms impede further assessment of signal quantity and information content. Consequently, in this study, a novel approach to suppress cross-terms is proposed. By extracting the WVD along the frequency slope direction, the extracted results undergo filtering via a window function and are subsequently multiplied by a summation suppression factor to further attenuate cross-terms and noise. Moreover, in this study, a comparative analysis of different window functions is conducted. Simulation experiments and practical data processing confirm the effectiveness of the proposed method in this study.

articleTitle: Kullback-Leibler Divergence Based Performace Evaluation of Geoacoustic Inverison Using Sources of Opportunity
abstract: In the realm of geoacoustic inversion problems, accurately estimating geoacoustic parameters is inherently challenging due to their sensitivity. The Bartlett estimator, used in a one-dimensional sensitivity analysis, evaluates the challenges associated with geoacoustic parameter inversion by establishing the relationship between the predicted acoustic field vector and the geoacoustic parameters in a deterministic manner. However, leveraging statistical sources of opportunity, statistical matching is preferred over the Bartlett estimator. This paper introduces the application of Kullback-Leibler divergence as a metric to evaluate array processing performance for geoacoustic parameter inversion, assessing the distinctions in probability distributions across acoustic fields. This metric is employed in the design of arrays in matched field geoacoustic inversion.

articleTitle: Wave Impedance Characteristics Based on Deep Sea Sound Vector Field
abstract: In this study, a deep sea sound vector field model is established under high-frequency approximation conditions based on ray theory and the Euler formula, focusing on the characteristics of the deep sea sound vector field. Analytical expressions for the particle velocity and wave impedance are also provided. The simulation of the sound vector field in two environments, range-independent and range-dependent, was carried out. As shown by the numerical analysis, the propagation characteristics of the sound pressure and horizontal particle velocity were basically consistent, whereas those of the sound pressure and vertical particle velocity varied considerably. The variation of horizontal wave impedance with range remains stable, whereas the vertical wave impedance fluctuates substantially with range, which indicates that the vertical wave impedance contains richer acoustic field information.

articleTitle: Research on Target Strength Characteristics of Multihighlights Model for Linear Array Acoustic Decoys
abstract: The spatial distribution characteristics of the target strength of the traditional multihighlight model are not evidently consistent with the variation law of the submarine target “butterfly figure.” There is a significant difference between the simulated model data and the measured submarine data. To address this problem, our study proposes an amplitude simulation method of target echo signal by introducing an equivalent radius scaling factor and random variables in the multihighlight model to improve the target echo signal simulation's fidelity of the linear-scale acoustic decoy in terms of target strength. The simulation results show that the improved multihighlight model is more consistent with the butterfly-shaped feature of target strength with azimuth variations. Simultaneously, the improved model reflects the uncertainty of multiple measurements at the same azimuth. This research provides a reference for implementing the simulation of target echo in linear array acoustic decoys and related fields in terms of fidelity.

articleTitle: Two-Dimensional Spectra for Multiple-Hydrophone Synthetic Aperture Sonar with Width Beam
abstract: The existing methods, which obtain two-dimensional spectra of the multiple-hydrophone synthetic aperture sonar (SAS), ignore the aperture dependence of the time during transmission and reception (TDTR) and the differential range curvature (DRC); therefore, its two-dimensional spectra do not have enough accuracy in the case of width beam. To address this problem, this paper proposes a new two-dimensional spectra. First, to achieve the aperture dependence of the TDTR, the exact slant range of each hydrophone is replaced by that of the slant range, which is the distance after the reference hydrophone shifted to the phase center of each hydrophone/transponder pair. Second, to obtain the DRC, the single square root term and the linear term of the approximated slant range are utilized as the basis functions to model the DRC, whose coefficients are solved by keeping the minimum error. Third, the two-dimensional spectra of the multiple-hydrophone SAS are developed by utilizing the stationary phase point to the proposed slant range of each hydrophone. Finally, the same simulation is conducted to test the validity of the proposed two-dimensional spectra.

articleTitle: A Passive Synthetic Aperture Direction-of-Arrival Estimation Method Under the Autonomous Underwater Vehicle Yaw Motion
abstract: When in motion, an autonomous underwater vehicle (AUV) will yaw under the influence of marine environment, and the direction-of-arrival (DOA) performance of the passive synthesis algorithm will be degraded. This study proposed a method for DOA estimation under the yaw motion. The method employed two-dimensional multiple signal classification algorithm to jointly estimate the yaw angle and azimuth. Subsequently, phase compensation was applied using the yaw angle to achieve accurate DOA estimation after aperture synthesis. Finally, various simulations were conducted to compare the performance of DOA estimation before and after considering the yaw angle. The results reveal that the proposed method can effectively improve the performance and resolution of DOA estimation.

articleTitle: A Method for Reducing the Measurement Frequency of Transducers in a Hydrostatic Water Vessel
abstract: Usually, the acoustic characteristics of transducers are calibrated in the free field. Affected by the boundary reflection in the free field region in a limited space, accurately calibrating its low-frequency performance is difficult. For deep-water transducers, the calibration of their acoustic performance is usually conducted in the laboratory using a special hydrostatic water vessel to simulate the deep-water environment. When considering a hydrostatic water vessel with an aperture of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\phi 4\ \mathrm{m}\times 12\ \mathrm{m}$</tex>, the lower limit of calibration frequency using the conventional tone burst method is 3 kHz in the vessel. In this study, to achieve acoustic performance calibration of emission transducers at lower frequencies, by analyzing the target characteristics of a transmitter, vessel water, and a receiver, as well as the estimation of transfer function between the transmitter and the receiver, a variable resolution time delay spectroscopy method is proposed. This method can effectively reduce the influence of reflection waves in limited water. The lower limit of the measurement frequency in the vessel is reduced, enabling the measurement of frequencies as low as 500 Hz in the existing water vessel.

articleTitle: Target Depth Classification Based on a Single Vector Hydrophone for Reliable Acoustic Paths in Deep Water
abstract: Depth classification of surface and underwater targets is helpful for rapid identification. The multipath arrival structure contains the position information of the target, which can be extracted for depth classification. Considering the vertical distribution of sound speed, this paper investigates the statistical relationship between the multipath time delay, vertical arrival angle, and target depth for a reliable sound path in a deep sea. Using composite hypothesis testing, a depth classification method using a single vector hydrophone is proposed. Herein, the multipath time delay between the direct and surface reflection waves is used as the test statistic, with the vertical arrival angle obtained from the ratio of the vertical and horizontal acoustic intensities from the signal recorded by a single vector sensor. The simulation results demonstrate that the proposed method is not sensitive to the horizontal distance of the target and can achieve good classification results at low signal-to-noise ratios.

articleTitle: Fully Distributed Fiber-Optic Hydrophone Cable for Acoustic Source Azimuth Estimation
abstract: This paper evaluates the azimuth estimation of an underwater acoustic source using a fully distributed fiber-optic hydrophone cable in Thousand Island Lake. Backscattering-enhanced optic fiber uniformly inscribed with backscattering-enhanced points was selected as the sensing fiber to improve the signal-to-noise ratio of the received signals. The distributed acoustic sensing system based on phase-sensitive optical time domain reflectometry was used to interrogate and demodulate the received signals to obtain the phase change along the cable. Frequency-domain beamforming was selected to process the demodulated signals and estimate the direction of arrival of the received signals. The cable's ability to detect static and moving acoustic sources was evaluated using various cable arrangement patterns. The results indicate that the cable is capable of detecting the acoustic source, showing that the proposed method has a great application potential in the marine field, such as underwater safety.

articleTitle: Moving Target Detection in Reverberation Background with Iterative Reweighted Least Squares Scheme
abstract: In this study, to address the issue of detecting moving targets in a reverberation environment, reducing reverberation by extracting the low-rank structure of multiframe data using the low-rank sparse decomposition theory is focused. Subsequently, successful detection of moving targets underwater was attained. To address the problem of low-rank matrix restoration, this study proposes a robust principal component analysis method using the Geman-McClure function and employs iterative reweighted least squares to it implement numerically. Experimental results verify that this method can accurately detect moving targets in a strong reverberation environment, which demonstrates clear advantages over traditional methods.

articleTitle: Dynamic Three-dimensional Ocean Sound Speed Field Reconstruction Using Bayesian Streaming Sparse Tensor Decomposition
abstract: Reconstructing a three-dimensional (3D) ocean sound speed field (SSF) from sparse and noisy measurements is crucial for various applications in ocean acoustics, including acoustic communication and target localization. Principles of classical SSF reconstruction algorithms (e.g., linear interpolation and geostatistical methods) are similar to those of machine learning theory, such as linear and Gaussian process regression. They can be uniformly regarded as supervised regression models, which learn the mapping from the geographical locations to the sound speed output. From a unified machine learning perspective, these supervised regression- based reconstruction approaches exhibit several limitations. They are sensitive to noise and incur high computational costs, requiring complete SSF reconstruction when updating partial sound speed data. Thus, online Bayesian learning is feasible to update the SSF. When a new batch of data is observed, dynamic SSF reconstruction occurs without requiring the integration of new data with old, ensuring that all observation data are used only once. To preserve the 3D structure of the SSF, Tucker decomposition is used to characterize the 3D SSF in the model, and a sparse prior is added to each element of the core tensor to reduce model complexity and the risk of overfitting. Numerical results obtained using real ocean SSF data demonstrate that the method performs excellently for dynamic SSF reconstruction.

Author Keywords: three dimensional sound speed field reconstruction

articleTitle: Three-Dimensional Passive Localization for Moving Targets Based on a Single Hydrophone
abstract: In this study, a three-dimensional passive localization method for moving targets based on a single hydrophone in shallow water is proposed. Due to the multipath effect in shallow waters, the broadband continuous signal, generated by a moving target, results in the superposition of multipath signals, which form stable interference fringes in the time-frequency domain. The trajectory equations of interference fringes for three-dimensional moving underwater targets are derived based on the ray theory. By constructing interference structure databases and applying matching algorithms, estimates of the target's velocity, and horizontal and vertical course angles are achieved, thereby facilitating target localization. Simulation experiments confirm the effectiveness of the proposed method, which provides a reliable basis for the three-dimensional passive localization of moving targets in shallow water waveguides.

articleTitle: Line Enhancement Algorithm Based on Unsupervised Deep Learning in Underwater Unmanned Vehicle
abstract: Underwater unmanned vehicles (UUVs) represent a typical passive sonar load and have been extensively used in military and civil fields domestically as well as internationally. For the passive sonar detection technology, it is important to filter out the useful line spectrum component in the signal from the received environmental noise and ship radiation nose. To realize the enhancement of the line spectrum component, the conventional adaptive line spectrum enhancer (adaptive line enhancer, ALE) has been widely utilized in passive sonar systems. Nevertheless, the ALE algorithm is quite different with respect to the input signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) feedback of the system, which is considerably worse in terms of robustness below a certain SNR threshold (approximately -10 Hz). To address this problem, in this study, a line spectrum component enhancement algorithm based on a deep neural network unsupervised neural network is proposed. Simulation experiments reveal that this algorithm that combines the modified least mean squares algorithm with the unsupervised neural network theory has great advantages in low-SNR environments.

articleTitle: Outer Field Surface Equivalent Source Method for Acoustic Radiation Structures in Sea-ice Waveguide
abstract: Considering the absence of effective methods for resolving the problem of large-scale structure acoustic radiation in sea-ice waveguide, an outer field surface equivalent source method is developed. The reflection coefficients of the two-layer ice-water interface are computed, the unknown strengths of the equivalent sources are computed using the mirror image method, and then, the reflection coefficients are used to calculate the cGreen's function of each equivalent source to the field point; the total acoustic field can be obtained by superimposing the acoustic fields of each equivalent source. The sound propagation of the benchmark model in an ideal waveguide with a two-layer ice sheet was computed using the outer field surface equivalent source and traditional equivalent source methods. The results reveal that the outer field surface equivalent source method can achieve high accuracy with a small number of equivalent sources.

articleTitle: Unitary Approximate Message Passing-Based Channel Estimation for OFDM Underwater Acoustic Communications
abstract: The approximate message passing (AMP) technique for channel estimation (CE) in underwater acoustic (UWA) communications has recently attracted considerable attention. As a member of the AMP family, the unitary AMP (UAMP) algorithm achieves robust performance by performing singular value decomposition on the measurement matrix before message passing is performed. Herein, we investigate the feasibility of UAMP-based CE for orthogonal frequency division multiplexing (OFDM) UWA communications. The experimental results showed that the UAMP-based CE scheme outperformed existing CE methods enabled by least squares or compressive sensing algorithms.

articleTitle: Line Spectrum Detection Technique Based on Joint Processing of Acoustic Pressure and Acceleration Signals from Vector Hydrophones
abstract: In the detection of line spectrum targets using vector hydrophones, acoustic pressure and particle velocity signals are commonly processed jointly to suppress isotropic noise and reduce the probability of false positives and negatives. Given that fiberoptic vector hydrophones acquire acceleration signals directly, obtaining particle velocity requires the integration of acceleration, which can lead to the accumulation or amplification of low-frequency noise and increase the computational load of the algorithm. This paper proposes a method that utilizes directly both acoustic pressure and acceleration signals in conjunction with adaptive local thresholds for the extraction of low-frequency line spectra. The effectiveness of the algorithm was validated through sea trial data. The algorithm achieved efficient extraction of target characteristic line spectra, enabling autonomous analysis and processing of underwater low-frequency line spectrum targets, which gives it a significant engineering application value.

articleTitle: Adaptive Feature Purification of Cavitation Noise Modulation Spectrum
abstract: To enhance the stability of modulation spectrum structure, in this study, a novel adaptive feature purification method called variational mode decomposition (VMD) combined with feature energy entropy (FEE) is proposed. First, to decompose the noise interference envelope into simple intrinsic mode functions (IMFs), the VMD algorithm is employed. Subsequently, to compute the weight space of the IMFs, the FEE algorithm is utilized. Finally, using the respective weights, the envelope signal is reconstructed, which leads to a further enhancement in the stability of the modulation spectrum. Both simulation and real data confirm the effectiveness of the VMD-FEE algorithm in feature purification of the modulation spectrum.

articleTitle: Design of a High-frequency Wideband Doppler Current Meter
abstract: This study presents the design of a high-frequency (HF) wideband Doppler current meter based on the principles of the acoustic Doppler effect. The Doppler current meter employs a complex autocorrelation algorithm to analyze the echo signals of HF acoustics emitted by its transducer, thereby deducing Doppler frequency shifts and subsequently computing the velocity of water currents in each direction. Compared with the low-frequency Doppler current meter, the HF wideband current meter has a lower measurement blind area and higher measurement resolution, although it has a more confined measurement range. To validate its performance, the velocity measurements of the HF wideband current meter were calibrated using a steady-flow circulating tank. Assessments against measurements from a narrowband Doppler current meter were also conducted. The results revealed high accuracy of the HF wideband Doppler current meter, with indication errors not exceeding 0.1 m/s.

articleTitle: Energy Threshold-Based Line Spectrum Extraction and Auxiliary Localization Method
abstract: In this study, a method named energy threshold-based line spectrum extraction and auxiliary localization is proposed in order to address the issue of false targets arising in multitarget cross-location. Initially, energy thresholds are set based on raw data from the time-frequency spectrum of tracking beams. Then, to assist in multitarget cross-location, the line spectrum information extracted through threshold discrimination is utilized, eliminating false targets and enhancing localization performance. Through simulation and the use of real data, this method can effectively extract line spectrum from the time-frequency spectrum of tracking beams under relatively high signal-to-noise ratio conditions. This approach, owing to its simplicity in computation and ease of obtaining prior information, holds high practical value in engineering.

articleTitle: Research on the Angle Distribution Characteristics of Submarine Target Strength
abstract: To enhance the accuracy of simulating submarine echoes using passive acoustic decoys, the target strength distribution of submarines must be understood deeper in three-dimensional space. In this study, the planar element method and Ts distribution model are employed to study the acoustic scattering characteristics of the Benchmark submarine model. The target strength in the two-dimensional case is extended to the three-dimensional case, and the statistical characteristics of its fluctuation distribution are attained. The statistical results reveal that the probability density value of three-dimensional target strength follows the Ts distribution. Subsequently, the trend of target intensity variation with azimuth and pitch angles is calculated, and the distribution parameters are analyzed. The results also show that the target strength fluctuates sharply with changes in azimuth and pitch angles. This study can provide a reference for the measurement and detection of acoustic reflection intensity of underwater submarine targets, as well as submarine countermeasures.

articleTitle: Influence of Physical Parameters on Echo Spectrum of Underwater Target
abstract: The elastic scattering features of the underwater target scattering wave depend on the physical parameters of the target, such as the material and structure. Intuitively evaluating the influence of the elastic scattering wave on the characteristics of the whole scattering wave signal is difficult due to the coupling and superposition of the elastic scattering wave and the geometric scattering wave of the target. Based on the different modulation characteristics of broadband echo spectrum produced by target geometry scattering and elastic scattering wave, this paper characterizes and studies the modulation features of echo spectrum and tests the influence of physical parameters on the echo spectrum of underwater target using several simple cylindrical targets with different physical parameters. Moreover, the geometric scattering wave and the elastic scattering wave of the simple target echo are extracted using the fractional Fourier transform (FrF<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$T$</tex>) domain filtering method, and the influence of physical parameters on the echo spectrum is quantitatively analyzed.

articleTitle: Research of Channel Polarization for Orthogonal Frequency Division Multiplexing Underwater Acoustic Communications
abstract: Construction and application of polar codes are dependent on the channel polarization phenomenon; presently, the research on the application of polar codes in underwater acoustic communication (UWC) is in the primary stage, and few relevant research has yet explored the underwater acoustic channel polarization phenomenon. This study extended the original channel polarization theory to the orthogonal frequency division multiplexing (OFDM) parallel UWC scenario. By simulating time-varying underwater acoustic channels in real communication environments, this study analyzed channel polarization phenomena including the distribution of the reliability parameters of the polarized subchannel and its changing law, after the incomplete channel polarization transformation, based on the Monte Carlo approximation method. Furthermore, this study investigated the effects of the underwater acoustic channel parameters, such as Doppler shift and spread, the multipath structure, and the channel time variation on the performance of the OFDM UWC system with channel polarization.

articleTitle: Physics-Informed Neural Networks for Solving Underwater Two-dimensional Sound Field
abstract: This paper proposes a fast computational method for underwater acoustic fields based on physics-informed neural networks (PINNs). By encoding the Helmholtz equation in the frequency domain, which represents the propagation laws of underwater sound, into physical neurons using automatic differentiation, and combining a small amount of measured data as information neurons, a physics-informed and data-driven neural network was constructed to solve the underwater acoustic fields. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed PINNs model can effectively solve the low-frequency shallow-water acoustic field computation problem. The results of our model are highly consistent with those obtained from traditional numerical models. Compared to purely data-driven models, the PINN model shows significant generalization ability and robustness, indicating promising engineering applications.

articleTitle: Robust DOA Estimation Method for Acoustic Vector Sensor Array Based on Element-Space Combination
abstract: The performance of the DOA estimation of standard Capon beamforming in an acoustic vector sensor array decreases sharply under the condition of steering vector mismatch. To overcome this problem, this paper proposes a robust beamforming algorithm based on the element-space combined processing of an acoustic vector array. The proposed algorithm extracts the beam transformation matrix of the traditional combined processing covariance matrix to the element-space and reconstructs the covariance matrix through singular value decomposition. Next, the singular value and vector complete the DOA estimation based on robust Capon beamforming. The simulation results show that the proposed method solves the spatial filtering problem of the traditional combined processing of acoustic pressure and particle velocity and has good spatial spectrum and target resolution abilities under the amplitude-phase error condition.

articleTitle: High Precision and Fast Calculation of Parametric Array Sound Fields Based on the Quasi-Monte Carlo Method
abstract: An efficient method for calculating the nonlinear sound field of a parametric array without additional approximation is proposed, which provides a new approach for calculating the sound field of a parametric array with complex sound sources. Quasilinear and successive approximations are used for the Westervelt equation. The difference-frequency sound-field solution for a parametric array is derived from the radiation of an infinite virtual source. Using the quasi-Monte Carlo method to solve the initial sound field, the limitation caused by additional approximation conditions can be avoided, and the spatial distribution of the virtual source density can be accurately and promptly obtained, thereby obtaining the distribution of the parametric array sound field. The radiated sound fields of two types of parametric array sound sources are calculated, and the superiority of the proposed method is verified.

articleTitle: Asymptotically Unbiased Target Motion Analysis Method Using Azimuth and Radial Velocity
abstract: In this study, an asymptotically unbiased target motion analysis method using azimuth and radial velocity is proposed. To calculate the target motion parameters under the condition that the target is observable, the constrained least squares method is employed. The effects of radial velocity error, azimuth error, and target initial distance on the performance of the algorithm proposed are analyzed. The simulation results reveal that with the increase of observation time, the distance and velocity estimation errors of the proposed algorithm gradually converge and tend to approach their respective Cramer-Rao lower bound, which has good robustness.

articleTitle: Modified High-resolution Receiver for Combining Signals of Frequency-modulated Waveforms
abstract: Frequency-modulated (FM) signals are frequently used in active sonar systems and have Doppler insensitivity, which is favorable for detection but not for delay-velocity coupling resolution. The combination signal based on FM waveforms processed via a high-resolution receiver (HRR) achieves high delay-velocity resolution and antireverberation compared to the traditional matched filter; however, it reduces the detection performance. In this paper, the nonlinear processing of an HRR is improved. Further, the signal-to-noise-ratio gain of subsegment processing is enhanced via a reasonable combination of subwaveforms, further improving the detection performance of the system. Simulation results show that the modified HRR improves the detection and antireverberation performance of the signal for practical applications under slight broadening of the resolution width.

articleTitle: Instantaneous Frequency Estimation of Noncooperative Underwater Acoustic Short-Pulse Signals Using the Peak of the STFT
abstract: This paper describes a time-frequency ridge line extraction method to estimate the instantaneous frequency (IF) of signals based on the peak of the short-time Fourier transform. The paper focuses on the combined underwater acoustic short-pulse signals under noncooperative conditions. The results of the preliminary IF estimation were improved using the iteratively reweighted least squares fitting algorithm. The IF estimation of signals reflects the signal parameters, including the start and end time, start and end frequency, pulse width, period, etc. It was possible to detect each sub-pulse of a combined pulse signal according to the IF estimation. In addition, a serial combined signal, parallel combined signal, and serial parallel signal in proper sequence were examined. Simulation results verify the feasibility and effectiveness of the proposed method in the presence of noise. This approach plays a prominent role in the estimation of the fine feature parameter for multi-component signals.

articleTitle: Node Degree Topology Control Routing Protocol Based on Weighted Link Quality Calculation
abstract: This research investigates the challenges of achieving efficient, reliable data transmission in underwater sensor networks (UWSNs) considering the unique underwater environment, which is characterized by channel fading, and the limited energy resources of nodes. These factors lead to data corruption and interruption. A node-degree topology control routing protocol (NDTCRP) is proposed to address these issues. The NDTCRP uses weighted link-quality computation to identify the optimal relay node and adjust the transmission power, particularly in high-node-density scenarios. The NDTCRP selects the optimal relay node according to residual energetic reserves and link quality with neighbor nodes, modulating the emission power as necessary to minimize energy consumption. Additionally, the protocol incorporates a communication void handling mechanism to address communication holes, ensuring the successful routing of data packets to their intended destinations. MATLAB simulation experiments substantiate the NDTCRP's significant efficacy in mitigating the overall energy expenditure and packet loss in underwater acoustic communication networks.

articleTitle: Improved Doppler Scale Estimation Based on Autocorrelation Function for Underwater Cyclic Prefix-Orthogonal Frequency Division Multiplexing Preamble
abstract: An enhanced Doppler estimation method that utilizes the phase of the autocorrelation function (ACF) is proposed in this study. The resolution of the Doppler scale estimation for the conventional autocorrelation method depends on the sampling rate of the received signal. By utilizing the phase of autocorrelation as a measurement, higher Doppler estimation accuracy without raising the sampling rate is achieved. However, the Doppler estimation range is limited to the induced phase ambiguity. A novel phase unwrapping method integrated with the Doppler scale factor is addressed to eliminate the phase ambiguity. The transmit signal considered in this study is cyclic prefix-orthogonal frequency division multiplexing preamble which satisfies the cyclic autocorrelation property, and the channel is modeled as each propagation path having a constant Doppler factor. Simulation results reveal that the proposed method achieves a performance gain of 10 dB compared with the conventional autocorrelation method and can be employed to obtain a large dynamic Doppler estimation range.

articleTitle: Single-channel Blind Source Separation Algorithm Based on Improved Variational Mode Decomposition
abstract: The single-channel blind source separation (SCBSS) algorithm based on variational mode decomposition (VMD) requires knowing the mode K in advance. An excessively large K value leads to excessive decomposition of the mixed signal, and an excessively small K value leads to underdecomposition of the mixed signal. To solve this problem, a SCBSS method based on the VMD of the Euclidean distance was proposed. First, the VMD method was used to decompose the observed mixed signals into two modes. Then, the Euclidean distance between the aforementioned two modes and the observed signal is calculated and averaged. The energy of a mode with a smaller Euclidean distance is calculated as a reference value. A loop body based on the Euclidean distance and energy value is constructed. In the loop, the number of source signals is determined, and the noise of the observed signals is removed to a certain extent. The proposed algorithm has broad application prospects in underwater acoustic fields.

articleTitle: Network Protocol Migration Framework: A Protocol Migration Framework for Underwater Network Based on NS3
abstract: Underwater information network research incorporates many cutting-edge technologies that greatly facilitate the optimal use of information-sharing resources, thereby remarkably improving the operational effectiveness of multiple military platforms. However, the inherent limitations of underwater acoustic channels, including limited communication bandwidth, notable multipath effects, and severe Doppler frequency shifts, have posed great challenges to the research of hydroacoustic communication networks. Nevertheless, current research on hydroacoustic communication networks remains at the level of theoretical simulation and lacks implementation on devices. In this study, an innovative framework that aims to smoothly migrate network protocols from simulation environments to hardware platforms is elaborated and proposed. The framework is based on existing simulation modules and cleverly develops several components that allow it to be directly adapted to real hydroacoustic modems without the need for remarkable modifications to the network protocol. In this study, the differences between simulation and experimental results for the same channel parameters are compared by performing common medium access control layer network simulations and experiments on the core board of a hydroacoustic modem, thus providing an in-depth validation of the superior performance of our framework. This result not only demonstrates the framework's ability to maintain consistency between simulated and real environments but also highlights its key potential and clear technological advantages in advancing the field of underwater network research.

articleTitle: Supersensitive Detector of Hydrosphere Pressure variations in Hydroacoustic Research
abstract: This paper describes the possibility of using a laser interference device as a hydroacoustic signal receiver. A supersensitive detector of hydrosphere pressure variations, created based on the equal-arm Michelson interferometer, was used in hydroacoustic studies. These experimental studies were conducted using hydroacoustic and seismoacoustic radiators as a signal source. A hypersensitive sensor of hydrosphere pressure variations was used as a signal radiator. The device received a signal from both hydroacoustic and seismoacoustic radiators.

Author Keywords: supersensitive detector of hydrosphere pressure variations

articleTitle: Sound Field Reconstruction of Plate Using Compressed Singular Value Decomposition Equivalent Source Method Combined with Generalized Inverse of Matrix
abstract: The near-field acoustic holography based on the equivalent source method is limited by array aperture and is only suitable for low-frequency acoustic field reconstruction. The compressed equivalent source method, based on the assumption of the sparsity of sound sources, has a wider analysis frequency band, but its accuracy is poor in terms of reconstructing the sound field of spatial continuous sound sources. In this study, a compressed singular value decomposition equivalent source method combined with generalized matrix (GIM-CSVDESM) is proposed, a set of basic functions is derived by combining the generalized inverse matrix principle with the compressed singular value equivalent source method, and the sparse reconstruction of the sound field is realized using this set of basic functions under the framework of the compressed equivalent source method. Numerical simulation reveals that GIM-CSVDESM has a high reconstruction accuracy for the sound field of the fixed plate and is less affected by the layout of the equivalent source. Finally, the correctness and effectiveness of GIM-CSVDESM are verified via the fixed plate experiment.

articleTitle: Underwater Transient Noise Duration Estimation Method Based on the Page Test
abstract: The underwater transient noise radiated by ships provides rich target information and is the focus of target acoustic characteristics analysis. The duration is a crucial representation parameter of the time-domain envelope. The Page test is an effective method for detecting transients, as it can be used to estimate the starting time of the transient. Hence, in this study, the ending time of the transient is estimated by performing time-domain reversal on the signal. In addition, in a low-signal-to-noise ratio environment, wavelet noise reduction pre-processing is introduced to improve the estimation effect and then to estimate the duration of transient noise. The simulation verification results reveal that this method can accurately estimate the duration of underwater transient noise and can also ensure high accuracy in low-signal-to-noise ratio environments.

articleTitle: Experimental Research on the Passive Positioning of Underwater Targets with Near-Field Precision
abstract: Compared with single-acoustic positioning technology, acoustic-magnetic passive positioning fusion technology improves the reliability and accuracy of underwater target positioning and can significantly enhance underwater information perception ability. The focused beamforming acoustic image passive location algorithm can precisely locate the target within a range of 600 m on both sides of the array. However, in practical applications, the algorithm is affected by multiple factors that reduce its accuracy, such as multipath effects, resulting in poor robustness for ultrashort-range locations. The magnetic field passive positioning algorithm, which uses magnetic field algorithm preprocessing and optimization search methods to solve target trajectory information, is not affected by the adverse factors of the shallow water environment and can achieve high-precision positioning with a precision of 0.1 ship length. However, this algorithm is affected by the rapid attenuation of the magnetic field. This paper utilizes the technology of focusing beam-forming acoustic image passive positioning and magnetic field passive positioning algorithm fusion to achieve high-precision and high-robustness passive positioning of the measured target in the near field. After extensive sea trial verification, in the application of a near-field linear array, the acoustic-magnetic passive positioning fusion algorithm can compensate for the problem of misjudgment in the direction of the incoming wave in acoustic positioning, effectively improving the accuracy of the passive positioning of underwater targets in the near field. The positioning accuracy of the measured target within a range of 60 m from the array body is better than that within a range of 3 m from the array body, and the positioning accuracy within a range of 60–600 m from the array body is better than that within a range of 5 m from the array body.

articleTitle: A Multiplatform Underwater Target Association and Tracking Method Based on Bearing and Frequency Measurements
abstract: In the field of underwater target information fusion, target association and tracking are tasks that are challenging to carry out. To address the problem of commonly used bearings-only target association and tracking algorithm, this study proposes a bearing-frequency target association and tracking algorithm. The proposed algorithm constructs an unbiased center frequency estimator and a hypothesis test criterion by introducing the nearest neighbor algorithm. Additionally, the algorithm fuses the bearing and frequency information, and a new target motion tracking model is established. On the one hand, the proposed algorithm adheres to the characteristic that different platforms observe the same target with the same center frequency, avoiding false targets. On the other hand, the unbiased center frequency estimator can estimate the center frequency, which addresses the problem of unknown center frequency in the traditional tracking algorithm. To verify the feasibility of the proposed algorithm, simulation and sea trials are carried out. The results reveal that the proposed algorithm has a good target association and tracking performance.

articleTitle: Automatic Target Tracking Based on the Multibeam Lofar Spectrum
abstract: To address the passive tracking problem of underwater targets, in this study, an automatic tracking method based on the multibeam Lofar spectrum is proposed. The tracking problem of multibeam Lofar spectrum targets is transformed into a correlation problem of tracking information. To predict and estimate the target motion trajectory, the Kalman filter algorithm is employed, and the target frequency-beam information is matched with the tracking trajectory. By upgrading the data association policy, the deleted target is reassociated, which effectively solves the target interruption problem to a certain extent. The actual data processing results reveal that the proposed method can effectively track the underwater target continuously, and the effectiveness of the proposed method is verified.

articleTitle: Research on the Direction of Arrival Methods Based on Nonuniform Linear Array in the Underwater Channels
abstract: The target azimuth estimation technology based on linear arrays has been widely applied. Higher array gain and higher azimuth resolution can be achieved by increasing the aperture of the array. For instance, laying a super large aperture linear array on the seabed can achieve high-precision azimuth estimation of distant targets. Owing to the uneven characteristics of the seabed, the large aperture array on the seabed is a nonuniform array. The azimuth estimation error is relatively large when traditional uniform array azimuth estimation techniques are applied to nonuniform array scenes. Therefore, in this study, a high-resolution azimuth estimation technique based on interpolation transformation is proposed to improve the azimuth resolution of nonuniform arrays. Analysis of sea trial data shows that the azimuth estimation technique based on interpolation transformation for nonuniform seabed has higher azimuth resolution than traditional uniform array azimuth estimation techniques.

articleTitle: Unsteady Narrowband Spectrum Enhancement Method of Ship Noise Using PSO and Stochastic Resonance Processing
abstract: To enhance the unsteady narrowband spectrum of ship noise, an unsteady narrowband stochastic resonance processing method based on particle swarm optimization (PSO) was proposed. The method adopts a bistable stochastic resonance model and takes the mean signal-to-noise ratio in the narrowband bandwidth as the fitness function; it can perform adaptive optimal selection of system parameters matching the narrowband spectrum and background noise and can enhance the narrowband spectrum signal. According to the flow of the algorithm, the simulated unsteady narrowband spectrum and the measured ship noise data are processed and analyzed. The results show that this method can easily adapt to the characteristics of the narrowband ship spectrum and enhances a weak narrowband spectrum; it has broad research prospects and good application value.

articleTitle: Experimental Investigation on Very-High-Rate Underwater Acoustic Communication
abstract: The demand for higher data rates and low-latency communication links has been increasing; hence, real-time very-high-rate underwater acoustic communication (UAC) has become more important. Previous coding modulation systems using decision-feedback equalization (DFE) receivers required period interleaving, which resulted in long throughput delay. To achieve low-delay real-time very-high-rate UAC, in this study, a two-stage DFE approach is proposed. In the first-stage, conventional DFE is employed to mitigate intersymbol interference, followed by the derivation of maximum ratio combining coefficients to enhance decoding accuracy through diversity combining. In the second stage, the low-delay decoding results are utilized as feedback for a noise-predictive DFE, effectively reducing the noise variance at the decoder input. In a horizontal UAC experiment at a depth of 630 m, using four-channel spatial multiplexing with 128 quadrature amplitude modulation (QAM) in the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$100\pm f5\text{kHz}$</tex> frequency band, a peak data rate of 350 kbps within a range of up to 200 m was achieved. Using 16-QAM, a peak data rate of 200 kbps within a range of up to 500 m was achieved.

articleTitle: Robust Equalizer for Joint Extended Preprocessing in Impulsive Noise
abstract: An important strategy for signal processing in impulsive noise environment is to first suppress the high amplitude mutations by a preprocessor and then use the signal processing method under Gaussian noise. This paper proposes an equalizer for joint impulsive noise extended preprocessing, which performs a nonlinear transform of received signals disturbed by impulsive noise, retaining more useful information while remaining robust. Combined with the sparse characteristics of the equalizer, the improved proportional stable fast transversal filter is then exploited to improve the convergence speed and reduce the equalization error. The results of underwater acoustic communication test in the Yellow Sea verify the superiority of the proposed method.

Author Keywords: improved proportional stable fast transversal filter

articleTitle: Smooth Normal Mode Theory in Rough Seabed Waveguides
abstract: This paper proposes a method for computing the normal mode eigenvalues and eigenvectors within waveguides characterized by rough seabed topography, employing the split-step Padé parabolic equation (PE) model. The PE matrix function is used to construct a regional propagation matrix for the rough seabed section. Subsequently, the propagation matrix for the entire propagation process is computed and subjected to smoothing. The matrix principal component analysis technique is used to derive the resultant smoothed normal modes. The novel approach is employed to systematically conduct numerical simulations of periodic undulating seabed ocean waveguides. The analysis encompasses the computation of normal mode eigenvalues, eigenvectors, and phase velocities under varying undulating parameters.

articleTitle: Study on the Properties of Acoustic Vector Field Near a Nonuniform-Thickness Baffle
abstract: Acoustic baffles are indispensable structures in underwater acoustic equipment, including underwater vehicles. It is often employed in the design of sonar arrays to reduce the self-noise of array carriers. Moreover, its design can enhance the sensitivity and directivity of the transducer to a certain extent. The study of underwater acoustic scattering of an acoustic baffle is a basic problem. In practice, the baffle thickness is usually uneven. To study the underwater acoustic scattering of a baffle and its near-field vector characteristics using ray acoustic theory, a model of the thickness of the baffle was established in this study. The results show that the vector sound field in front of the baffle is affected by the incident sound wave and the baffle parameters. Finally, the same model was calculated using COMSOL, and the results agreed with the theoretical results.

articleTitle: Underwater Target Length Prediction Method Based on Deep Learning
abstract: The echo received by active sonar contains valuable and crucial information regarding underwater targets. The scale or the length of the target, which can be estimated from the time broadening of the echo, is one of the key features for underwater target classification and recognition. This paper introduces a method for predicting the length of underwater targets using a deep neural network. The deep neural network is constructed, which is used to first extract features with a backbone network. The region of the target echo envelope is then regressed through a one-dimensional bounding box to align with the start and end points of the ground truth. Experiment results showed that the proposed method yields visually intuitive outcomes for target length prediction, increasing the interpretability of the neural network. The prediction accuracy of the proposed method was better than that of the traditional peak search method, especially under low signal-to-noise ratio conditions.

articleTitle: Design and Simulation of a Low-Frequency Piezoelectric Spherical Hydrophone
abstract: Nuclear explosions, earthquakes, tsunamis, and volcanic eruptions will all produce high-intensity infrasound waves. To better detect infrasound signals in water, highly sensitive hydrophones with good low-frequency characteristics must be developed. In this study, a low-frequency spherical hydrophone is proposed due to the excellent pressure resistance characteristics of its structure. Moreover, through modeling and simulation, the pressure resistance performance and low-frequency sensitivity of the hydrophone in the deep sea were discussed. The results indicate that the hydrophone can effectively complete infrasound detection tasks in the deep sea.

articleTitle: Q-Learning-Based Energy-Efficient Routing Protocol for Underwater Wireless Sensor Networks
abstract: Underwater wireless sensor networks (UWSNs) have garnered considerable attention in recent years. Subject to constraints such as fixed node locations, limited energy, and harsh communication environments, designing high-performance routing protocols becomes crucial. Herein, we propose a Q-learning-based energy-efficient routing (QEER) protocol for UWSNs. To be specific, the reward function of Q-learning is designed by incorporating the energy, distance, and redundancy factors. Different from existing works ignoring redundant nodes in routing design, we exploit redundant nodes as relay nodes to extend the lifetime of UWSNs. In addition, the Time Division Multiple Access and Code Division Multiple Access protocols are reasonably implemented. Simulations demonstrate that compared with conventional clustering algorithms, the proposed QEER protocol achieves substantial improvements in terms of node lifetime, energy consumption, and the amount of forwarded data.

articleTitle: Passive Location of Shallow Sea Targets Based on Scalar and Vector Hydrophone Association
abstract: In this study, a location algorithm that combines a ternary equilateral plane array composed of scalar hydrophone with a single vector hydrophone was designed in order to address the problem that a single vector hydrophone cannot be located, the measurement bandwidth of which is too narrow. The positioning formula of a ternary equilateral array is derived, and the impact of time delay errors on the accuracy of the positioning formula is analyzed. The advantages of the three formulas in specific angular ranges are determined. The accurate direction finding and ranging are completed by combining vector hydrophones. To automatically screen out the defects, a “circular sieve” is introduced for real-time post-processing. In the sea experiment, under the interference of shallow sea environmental noise, the location of the stationary and dynamic targets has been realized. Compared with the single-vector hydrophone, the proposed algorithm is more accurate. It has a good location effect in the horizontal plane and has a certain engineering application value.

articleTitle: Edge Processing for Calculating the Acoustic Radiation of Underwater Structures using the Boundary Element Method
abstract: Herein, the influence of edges on the results and the processing method of edge are studied when a boundary element is used to calculate the sound field of an underwater structure with edges. Because the edge is the intersection line of two different smooth planes, there is no definition of a normal vector at the edge of the edge; however, the boundary element method needs to give the normal vibration velocity of the node at the edge of the edge when calculating the sound field, and the node at the edge of the edge has a different normal vibration velocity for different elements. If they are separated, the dimension of the node's normal vibration velocity column vector will be greater than that of the node's sound pressure column vector. Herein, an approximation method for edges is presented on the basis of the idea of element superposition in the finite element method and the results of the program calculations of different processing methods are compared with the simulation results. The results show that the approximation method is in good agreement with the simulation results, and when the load is distributed on the edge, different processing methods have a great influence on the calculation results, with a maximum error of 9.56 dB.

articleTitle: Fast Automatic Detection of Active Sonar Target Echo Based on Constant-False-Alarm Rate
abstract: In traditional active sonar detection, a sonar operator detects the target echo using their naked eyes; the operator is easily tired and cannot meet the development requirements of an unmanned underwater vehicle. The pulse width of a transmitted signal corresponds to the length of echo detection data in time dimension when echo detection is performed using short-time Fourier transform. Using the constant-false-alarm detection method, this paper detects the azimuth spectrum of each quick snap with a constant false alarm, obtains the length of the target echo in the time dimension by accumulating the multisnap accumulative vector, and combines the multidimensional feature information for discrimination to realize fast automatic detection of the active sonar target echo. The effectiveness of the proposed method was verified using simulation and experimental data, and the algorithm was easy to implement in engineering.

articleTitle: Reducing Beam Cross-coupling Errors in Acoustic Doppler Sonar by Phase Modulation
abstract: Interference between beams can lead to inaccurate velocity estimates in Doppler sonar. To improve navigation or current measurement accuracy, eliminating beam cross-coupling errors is essential. This study investigates the relationship between the Doppler phases of actual echoes and those of the main lobe and sidelobe echoes, including the associated coupling power. Considerably, a signal processing method employs phase modulation of the transmitted signals. The proposed method leverages the relationship between the signal autocorrelation function and Fourier coefficients. Results show that the frequency estimation errors of the phase modulation method are notable lower than those of currently employed signal processing methods under various power conditions.

articleTitle: Zynq-Based Signal Processing System for Imaging Sonar
abstract: This paper presents the design of a Zynq-based imaging sonar signal processing system, with the aim to overcome the technical challenges associated with high integration, multichannel high-speed sampling, and real-time signal processing in traditional imaging sonar systems. The field-programmable gate array controls the synchronized sampling of multichannel signals and the real-time processing of sonar signals, while the ARM handles the network transmission of sonar image data and system control. This program offers remarkable scalability and flexibility, with promising potential for various applications.

articleTitle: Self-Interference Suppression of Full-Duplex Spread Spectrum Underwater Acoustic Communication Based on CSK Modulation
abstract: To solve the bandwidth limitation and improve the utilization rate of the frequency band in underwater acoustic communication, this study introduced full-duplex (FD) underwater acoustic communication. Spread spectrum communication is a common communication system in underwater acoustic communication. However, the main problem in FD communication is the influence of self-interference (SI) on the demodulation of the expected signal. The communication rate of direct sequence spread spectrum itself is low, and one of the ways to improve the rate is to use the code shift keying (CSK) modulation. In this paper, a method of suppressing SI in the code domain was introduced for CSK-modulated spread spectrum communication. Through the hyperspace cancellation by coordinate zeroing (HCCO) algorithm, SI was suppressed and the FD communication rate and communication effect were improved. Specifically, for the signals with the same frequency simultaneously and for differential joint CSK-modulated spread spectrum underwater acoustic communication, the HCCO algorithm suppressed the SI, detected the symbol bit information of the signal through differential energy, and demodulated each symbol to obtain the CSK mapping information. In this study, the ability of the algorithm to suppress SI was verified through simulation. When the signal-to-noise ratio is 5 dB and the signal-to-interference ratio is -20dB, the bit error rate is less than 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">––3</sup>.

articleTitle: Classification Method for Surface and Underwater Targets Based on Target Acoustic Field Vertical Wave Number Filtering
abstract: This paper proposes a surface and underwater target discrimination method based on vertical wave number spectrum filtering of the acoustic field combined with the theory of normal mode wave and wave number integral. The vertical wave number spectrum of the acoustic field is estimated based on the dispersion transform, which solves the problem that the two-dimensional fast Fourier transform (2D-FFT) cannot use the nonequal interval matrix to estimate the target acoustic field wave number spectrum. By demodulating the envelope characteristics of the vertical wave number spectrum, the target depth information is obtained to realize the classification and discrimination of underwater targets.

articleTitle: Underwater Acoustic Target Recognition based on Preemphasis Filter Convolutional Neural Network
abstract: N owadays, underwater acoustic target recognition (UATR) is a core technology in underwater acoustics. Identifying the underwater target from the complex marine background noise is critical to gain an acoustic advantage in underwater confrontation. To tackle the problem at its source, this paper proposes a deep learning model to improve target recognition capability based on the convolutional neural network (CNN) model with a preemphasis filter (PEF) module (herein presented as PEF+CN <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$N$</tex> model). This model learns the fluctuations and differences between ship targets and multiple marine background noises. It then enhances the time-frequency spectrum quality and the signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) in a data-driven way. Finally, comparative experiments were conducted to validate the improvements of the proposed model. The results showed that the spectral feature is more pronounced than the original condition. Moreover, the overall and the single-class recognition accuracy also increased compared with the same CNN model without PEF, confirming the intelligence of the proposed model and offering the feasibility for more practical engineering applications.

articleTitle: Particle Swarm Optimization Algorithm for Speed Estimation Based on Azimuth and Doppler Information
abstract: Autonomous underwater vehicles (AUVs) have been used widely in the field of marine engineering owing to their flexibility and portability. Monitoring the speed condition of AUVs is essential to ensure their high precision operation. This paper develops a speed estimation model based on azimuth and Doppler shift, provides a geometric analytical solution, and proposes an AUV instantaneous speed estimation method based on particle swarm optimization. Finally, experiments are performed to verify the effectiveness of the algorithm. In the node baseline and its vicinity, the estimation error based on particle swarm optimization is much smaller than the geometric analytical solution.

articleTitle: Automatic Tracking Algorithm for Periodic Pulse Signal Based on Central Difference Kalman Filter
abstract: To address the problem that the traditional tracker was unable to maintain tracking when there were some missing pulses of periodic pulse signals, in this study, an automatic tracking algorithm for periodic pulse signals based on a central difference Kalman filter (CDKF) was proposed. Based on the actual situation in the application of sonar pulse reconnaissance, the target distance was relatively far with a limited bearing change rate, so using bearing and bearing change rate, two-dimensional linear motion and observation equation models were established. Then, an automatic start method of pulse tracking was presented. The method was based on pulse sameness discrimination. When the number of identical pulses exceeded the specified number, a tracker was started. Then, based on CDKF tracking, to predict and filter target bearing smoothly utilizing the established motion and observation equations, the automatic tracking procedure was presented. When there was a missing bearing observation in the input detection sequence, the predicted bearing value was used as a tracked one. When the signals could be detected again, the CDKF algorithm was operated using the relation between the predicted values and the current observations to maintain the tracking of the target. If the number of successive pulse deficiencies exceeded the specified, the tracking procedure was ended. Finally, simulation results of several situations with missing some stochastic pulses revealed that the effects of CDKF and KF had no significant difference on tracking even bearing change rate target. Moreover, although under linear motion and observation equation models, the effect of CDKF was better than KF on tracking dynamic bearing change rate targets. In the scenario of sonar pulse reconnaissance, adopting simple two-dimensional linear equations could ensure the effectiveness of tracking and avoid complicated calculations caused by nonlinear models.

articleTitle: Channel Estimation for OTFS Underwater Acoustic Communications via Vector Approximate Message Passing
abstract: Herein, we explore the feasibility of channel estimation via vector approximate message passing (VAMP) algorithm for orthogonal time frequency space underwater acoustic (UWA) communications. To make use of the sparsity of the UWA channel in the delay-Doppler domain, Bernoulli-Gaussian prior distribution was used. The numerical and experimental results were provided to demonstrate the performance of the VAMP-based channel estimation scheme. It showed that the proposed scheme outperforms traditional channel estimation methods governed by least squares or linear minimum mean square error criteria.

articleTitle: Recognition of Underwater Acoustic Chirp Imitation Whistle Communication Signals Based on Improved-ResNet
abstract: Currently, underwater bionic communication signal-recognition methods based on pattern recognition exhibit poor environmental adaptability and insufficient robustness. Considering the application of deep learning in the field of modulation recognition of communication signals, this study designs a deep learning network assisted by an attention mechanism and proposes a recognition method for underwater acoustic chirp simulated Whistler communication signals. First, the time-frequency contour of the input signal is extracted using a dynamic adaptive threshold segmentation method. Second, an attention mechanism was introduced to enhance the detailed feature extraction capability of the deep residual network. Subsequently, a transfer learning network training method is used to enhance the robustness of the model. Finally, the validity and robustness of the proposed method is analyzed through numerical simulation and lake experiments. The results demonstrate that the proposed method achieves over 90% recognition accuracy in simulated underwater channels with signal-to-noise ratio greater than -15 dB, and 98.7<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">%</sup> recognition accuracy in the lake experiments. Compared with existing methods, the proposed method demonstrated superior robustness in complex underwater environments.

articleTitle: Impact Analysis of Sea Ice Stratification on the Propagation Characteristics of Guided Waves in Ice
abstract: Based on elastic-wave theory, the dispersion curves of ice-guided waves in single-layered and double-layered ice are obtained via theoretical calculations and verified using simulations. Using variations in the phase velocity dispersion curves and attenuation coefficients, the influence of ice stratification on the propagation characteristics of ice-guided waves was analyzed. The results indicate that the vertical stratification of sea ice significantly affects the phase velocity and attenuation coefficient of most ice-guided wave propagation. Nevertheless, the quasi-Scholte wave and low-frequency M3 wave exhibits slight changes due to sea ice stratification, the phase velocity curve is practically unchanged, and the attenuation coefficients are always close to O. This implies that the quasi-Scholte wave and low-frequency M3 wave can propagate over long distances in stratified sea ice, and their waveform is sufficiently stable to be easily recognized.
